When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster. We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI. We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services. If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe. About This Role: Crusoe’s marketing team is scaling fast, and Marketing Operations sits behind almost everything it ships: event follow-up, product launches, gated content, credit campaigns and partner programs. As our Marketing Operations Intern, you’ll work directly with the Marketing Operations lead. You’ll help build, QA and run the campaigns and data processes that turn the team’s work into pipeline for a growing sales organization. This is a real seat on the team. Your work will go live in Marketo and Salesforce, and the projects you own will still be in use after you leave. This role is for someone curious and detail-oriented who likes building things and wants to see how B2B marketing works behind the scenes. You don’t need to know Marketo yet. You do need to be the kind of person who reads ahead, asks good questions and gets excited when a messy dataset finally comes out clean. This is a paid, full-time, 12-week summer internship for 2027, in office in San Francisco or Bellevue. What You’ll Be Working On: Campaign builds and QA: Build and test email programs, landing pages and forms in Marketo for launches, events and nurture emails and then check them before they go out. Event and lead data: Clean, normalize and import attendee and lead lists from events and partners into Marketo and Salesforce, so follow-up goes out fast and to the right people. Data quality: Find and fix duplicates, missing fields and bad values, and help keep our database clean as volume grows. Tracking and reporting: Keep UTMs consistent and help build the reports that show which campaigns drive pipeline. AI-assisted tooling: Use AI tools to automate repetitive ops work, such as data cleanup, QA checklists and documentation, and help make the whole team faster. Process documentation: Write clear how-tos and runbooks for the processes you learn, so the next person can pick them up quickly. Capstone project: Own one meaningful project from scoping to delivery, such as lead scoring analysis, an attribution deep-dive or a tool evaluation, and present the results to marketing leadership at the end of the summer. What You’ll Bring to the Team: Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Business, Information Systems, Data/Analytics or a related field, graduating in December 2027 or by Spring 2028. 0–1 years of professional experience. A previous internship, campus role or part-time job involving data, marketing or operations is a plus, but not required. Strong Excel or Google Sheets skills: lookups, pivot tables, cleaning and reformatting messy data. Close attention to detail. You catch the broken link or the wrong segment before it ships. Curiosity and initiative. You dig into new tools on your own and ask questions without being prompted. Clear written and verbal communication, and comfort working with several teams at once. Able to work in an office, in San Francisco or Bellevue for the full 12 weeks. Bonus Points: Hands-on experience with Marketo, HubSpot, Salesforce or another marketing automation tool or CRM. Basic SQL, Python or experience building with AI tools. Interest in AI infrastructure or cloud computing. Coursework or projects in data analytics, marketing analytics or experimentation. Our Internship Program Our 12-week, in-person program pairs high-impact work with one-on-one mentorship and direct access to leaders across the organization. You'll gain hands-on experience that goes beyond the classroom. The program is built to support your professional growth and help you forge valuable connections within Crusoe and beyond. We're looking for motivated, talented people who are eager to take on real responsibility and make a real impact. Are you ready to join the Future Cru? 2027 Summer Internship Dates (choose one cohort): May 24 – August 13, 2027 June 14 – September 3, 2027 Crusoe is not sponsoring visas for these positions at this time or in the future. If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe. About the Role: Crusoe's Managed AI team builds the services customers use to customize and run large language models without managing infrastructure. On the training side, it's a post-training platform where customers adapt models to their own data with supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL). On the inference side, it's managed serving that runs open-weight and fine-tuned models, including LoRA adapters, fast and cost-efficiently on Crusoe's GPU fleet. The two are closely connected: models trained on the platform are deployed and served on the same infrastructure, and RL training depends on high-throughput inference for rollouts. As an AI Applied Research PhD Intern, you'll own a research question somewhere on that path from training to serving. It could be making RL work reliably on real customer tasks, or making inference faster and cheaper without losing quality. You'll run experiments on frontier open-weight models (Qwen, GLM, DeepSeek and Kimi-class models) on large GPU clusters, turn your findings into recipes and platform features that customers use, and present the results to the team and leadership. This is a 12-week, full-time, in-person internship. Candidates who want to see their research run in production, not just in a paper, will find it a good fit. What You'll Bring to the Team: Education: Currently enrolled in a PhD program in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Electrical Engineering or a related field, with an expected graduation date between Fall 2027 and Spring 2029. Research experience: 2+ years of research experience in machine learning or ML systems, including hands-on work with large language models: training or fine-tuning (SFT, RLHF, DPO, GRPO/PPO) or inference optimization. Programming: Strong Python and PyTorch; comfortable reading and modifying large ML codebases. Experimental rigor: You design controlled experiments, choose the right baselines and metrics, and can tell a real effect from noise. Systems awareness: Working knowledge of how LLM training and inference run on GPUs, such as batching, memory, mixed precision and parallelism. Communication: You explain complex results clearly in writing and in person, and you work well with engineers turning research into product. Bonus Points Publications at venues such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, MLSys, ACL, EMNLP or COLM on RL for LLMs, reward modeling, agents, efficient training or efficient inference. Hands-on experience with inference engines (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM) or training frameworks (verl, OpenRLHF, TRL, Megatron-LM, DeepSpeed). Experience with quantization, speculative decoding, GPU kernels (CUDA, Triton) or LoRA/PEFT methods. Experience building agent environments, tool-use sandboxes or evaluation harnesses. Open-source contributions to Training/Infernece libraries. description: About Basis Basis is a nonprofit applied AI research organization with two mutually reinforcing goals. The first is to understand and build intelligence. This means to establish the mathematical principles of what it means to reason, to learn, to make decisions, to understand, and to explain; and to construct software that implements these principles. The second is to advance society’s ability to solve intractable problems . This means expanding the scale, complexity, and breadth of problems that we can solve today, and even more importantly, accelerating our ability to solve problems in the future. To achieve these goals, we’re building both a new technological foundation that draws inspiration from how humans reason, and a new kind of collaborative organization that puts human values first. About the Role Research interns work closely with scientists and engineers at Basis, learning from and contributing to our team. Internships are open to graduate-level candidates (or equivalent), pursuing research in technical and scientific domains, including areas of computer science such as machine learning, and programming languages. We are looking for people who want to grow technically and who value gaining a deeper understanding of concepts at their foundations. We expect you to: Have demonstrated an ability to do high-quality scientific research. Possible ways to demonstrate this include publications, technical reports, and software projects In addition, the following would be an advantage: Excited about solving real world problems and having positive societal impact Activities Develop and explore computational theories of intelligence, including reasoning, learning, and decision-making In close collaboration with domain experts inside and especially outside Basis, work as a team member to help solve scientific and societal problems Distill insights from solving problems into more general mathematical and computational theories Contribute to open-source software (Optionally) Publish and present findings in journals and conferences Contribute to the culture and direction of Basis Potential projects Interns will be placed with one of our active challenge projects or our core tech team , according to project needs and intern fit. In particular, we have openings within the following areas, but this list is not exhaustive: Dynamical Systems + Machine Learning at Basis We’re seeking interns interested in developing the theory and methods that let us learn how systems work from data—and quantify what we don’t know. This work sits at the intersection of machine learning, dynamical systems, and uncertainty quantification , with the goal of advancing how we represent, infer, and forecast complex real-world processes under uncertainty. Projects may be theoretical (developing foundations for learning and reasoning about dynamics), methodological or engineering-focused (building and integrating algorithms into our universal reasoning engine), or applied (using our existing toolkits to study systems such as animal behavior and robot co-design ). Recent blogpost: Introducing Dynestyx, a probabilistic programming library for dynamical systems Interns should have familiarity with differential equations , machine learning , and Bayesian inference . Secure Sensing & Robotics We are starting a new hardware research effort on privacy-centered hardware. The ubiquity of IoT devices and never-ending appetite of large-scale AI models have normalized mass data recording and mining of public and private spaces. This motivates numerous research questions: (1) how do we design public interest IoT and robotics applications that preserve community members’ privacy? (2) How can we design checks and balances in sensing systems to affirm compliance with consent and anti-eavesdropping laws? (3) How do we center trustworthiness in the design of IoT and robotic system? We are looking for candidates with experience in at least one of the following: embedded systems, edge computing, robotics, machine learning, security, and computer vision. Please feel free to reach out to learn more about the latest work. Formal Methods and Verification Basis is building infrastructure for machine-checkable trust in scientific software and autonomous systems. Our aim is to make it practical to express what a system should do, verify that it does it, and maintain that evidence as the system evolves. Recent blogposts: Synthesizing Rollback Systems for Safer Agents , Ship your interpreter , Using LLM-based verification to eliminate bugs in Linux's network stack . Collaborative Intelligent Systems We study collaborative intelligent systems in the wild, focusing on how social species coordinate, communicate, and adapt in complex environments. Our work spans multiple levels of behavior, from fine-grained group foraging and navigation decisions to city-scale ecological and evolutionary dynamics. Using multimodal data (audio, video, environmental, and genetic), we develop probabilistic and dynamical systems models that investigate how communication and cooperation shape resilience in changing ecosystems. Interns will contribute to data analysis, modeling, or field data collection for our “behavioral weather station” network monitoring social species across cities. Recent blogposts: Reconstructing animal movements in 3D naturalistic environments from field measurements , The hidden sounds of rats: A new way to hear urban wildlife Key skills: interest in animal behavior or collective systems; experience with data science, machine learning. Preference will be given to candidates with experience in at least one of the following areas: dynamical systems modeling, multimodal data analysis, multi-agent simulation. description: THE CARWOW GROUP Carwow Group is driven by a passion for getting people into cars. But not just any car, the right car. That’s why we are building the go-to destination for car-changing. Designed to reach drivers everywhere with our trail-blazing portfolio of personality rich automotive brands; Carwow, Auto Express, evo, Driving Electric and Car Buyer. What started as a simple reviews site, is now one of the largest online car-changing destinations in Europe - over 10m customers have used Carwow to help them buy and sell cars since its inception. Last year we grew over 50% with nearly £3bn worth of cars bought on site, while £1.8bn of cars were listed for sale through our Sell My Car service. In 2024 we went big and acquired Autovia, doubling our audience overnight. Together we now have one of the biggest YouTube channels in the world with over 1.1 billion annual views, sell 1.2 million print copies of our magazines and have an annual web content reach over 350million. WHY JOIN US? Shortlisted in the prestigious Culture 100 list of the top Growth companies to work for by Hyer; we also recently raised $52m in funding led by global venture capital firm an early backer of LinkedIn and Shopify, Bessemer Venture Partners, to accelerate our growth plans! As pioneers, we’re always driving for new territory and positive change, so our work as a group is never done. Where others see difficulty, it’s our responsibility to see possibility – building new experiences, launching new titles and listening to drivers. Being a part of Carwow Group means championing drivers and the automotive industry, acting as a disrupter and never being afraid to fail (but learning fast when we do!). Our team of 500 employees across the UK, Germany, Spain and Portugal are revolutionising car-changing and we are fast expanding our mission across every single brand and country we operate in, so jump in! THE ROLE Carwow knows what millions of Spaniards are looking for when they buy a new car: which models they configure, which brands they compare and when they're ready to buy. Our OEM & Media team uses that first-party data to help car brands and their media agencies reach buyers at the right moment, through advertising, data and lead generation. As our intern you'll support the whole team, from the commercial side (preparing pitches, data and insights for brands and agencies) to operations (getting campaigns live and reporting on how they perform). It's a hands-on role. You'll learn how automotive brands make decisions, how digital media is sold and how data turns into business. WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING Sales support: build and polish client decks and proposals in Google Slides, working with the Partnerships Managers. Data & insights: pull and analyse marketplace data (configurations, enquiries, brand and model demand) to back up proposals and account plans. Campaign operations: help the Operations team receive and check creatives, set up campaigns and track delivery. Reporting: prepare campaign performance reports and post-campaign analyses for brands and agencies. Market research: keep track of brands, launches, competitors and trends in the Spanish car market. CRM: keep Salesforce and the pipeline up to date. AI in practice: use AI tools every day to speed up analysis, reporting and deck building, and help the team find new ways to use them. WHAT YOU'LL NEED Student or recent graduate in Business, Marketing, Economics, Data or similar. Strong Google Sheets / Excel skills (pivot tables, lookups, formulas). You enjoy working with numbers. Good at building clear, well-designed slides. You can turn data into a story. Hands-on experience with AI tools (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or similar) as part of how you work, not just something you've tried. Organised and detail-oriented, able to juggle requests from different people. Curious about the car industry and digital advertising. Fluent in Spanish, good working English (part of the interview will be in English). Nice to have: Salesforce/HubSpot, SQL or Looker, design tools (Canva/Adobe). WHAT'S IN IT FOR YOU A 6 months internship with appropriate remuneration A steep learning curve that will help you advance both personally and professionally Great development opportunities in a fast-growing startup Flexible working: 3x/week in our Madrid office We also have a new ‘work from anywhere for a month each year' policy in place should you wish to use it Social: company wide collaboration such as bi-weekly product demos, coffee with the exec sessions, culture club, and lots of fun in our team events! Diversity and inclusion is an integral part of our culture. We know that diverse teams are strong teams, so we welcome those with alternative identities, backgrounds, and experiences to apply for this position. We make recruiting decisions based on experience, skills and potential, so all our applicants are treated fairly and equally. #LI-RV1

The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI. We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services. If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe. About This Role: Crusoe’s marketing team is scaling fast, and Marketing Operations sits behind almost everything it ships: event follow-up, product launches, gated content, credit campaigns and partner programs. As our Marketing Operations Intern, you’ll work directly with the Marketing Operations lead. You’ll help build, QA and run the campaigns and data processes that turn the team’s work into pipeline for a growing sales organization. This is a real seat on the team. Your work will go live in Marketo and Salesforce, and the projects you own will still be in use after you leave. This role is for someone curious and detail-oriented who likes building things and wants to see how B2B marketing works behind the scenes. You don’t need to know Marketo yet. You do need to be the kind of person who reads ahead, asks good questions and gets excited when a messy dataset finally comes out clean. This is a paid, full-time, 12-week summer internship for 2027, in office in San Francisco or Bellevue. What You’ll Be Working On: Campaign builds and QA: Build and test email programs, landing pages and forms in Marketo for launches, events and nurture emails and then check them before they go out. Event and lead data: Clean, normalize and import attendee and lead lists from events and partners into Marketo and Salesforce, so follow-up goes out fast and to the right people. Data quality: Find and fix duplicates, missing fields and bad values, and help keep our database clean as volume grows. Tracking and reporting: Keep UTMs consistent and help build the reports that show which campaigns drive pipeline. AI-assisted tooling: Use AI tools to automate repetitive ops work, such as data cleanup, QA checklists and documentation, and help make the whole team faster. Process documentation: Write clear how-tos and runbooks for the processes you learn, so the next person can pick them up quickly. Capstone project: Own one meaningful project from scoping to delivery, such as lead scoring analysis, an attribution deep-dive or a tool evaluation, and present the results to marketing leadership at the end of the summer. What You’ll Bring to the Team: Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Business, Information Systems, Data/Analytics or a related field, graduating in December 2027 or by Spring 2028. 0–1 years of professional experience. A previous internship, campus role or part-time job involving data, marketing or operations is a plus, but not required. Strong Excel or Google Sheets skills: lookups, pivot tables, cleaning and reformatting messy data. Close attention to detail. You catch the broken link or the wrong segment before it ships. Curiosity and initiative. You dig into new tools on your own and ask questions without being prompted. Clear written and verbal communication, and comfort working with several teams at once. Able to work in an office, in San Francisco or Bellevue for the full 12 weeks. Bonus Points: Hands-on experience with Marketo, HubSpot, Salesforce or another marketing automation tool or CRM. Basic SQL, Python or experience building with AI tools. Interest in AI infrastructure or cloud computing. Coursework or projects in data analytics, marketing analytics or experimentation. Our Internship Program Our 12-week, in-person program pairs high-impact work with one-on-one mentorship and direct access to leaders across the organization. You'll gain hands-on experience that goes beyond the classroom. The program is built to support your professional growth and help you forge valuable connections within Crusoe and beyond. We're looking for motivated, talented people who are eager to take on real responsibility and make a real impact. Are you ready to join the Future Cru? 2027 Summer Internship Dates (choose one cohort): May 24 – August 13, 2027 June 14 – September 3, 2027 Crusoe is not sponsoring visas for these positions at this time or in the future. About the Role: Crusoe's Managed AI team builds the services customers use to customize and run large language models without managing infrastructure. On the training side, it's a post-training platform where customers adapt models to their own data with supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL). On the inference side, it's managed serving that runs open-weight and fine-tuned models, including LoRA adapters, fast and cost-efficiently on Crusoe's GPU fleet. The two are closely connected: models trained on the platform are deployed and served on the same infrastructure, and RL training depends on high-throughput inference for rollouts. As an AI Applied Research PhD Intern, you'll own a research question somewhere on that path from training to serving. It could be making RL work reliably on real customer tasks, or making inference faster and cheaper without losing quality. You'll run experiments on frontier open-weight models (Qwen, GLM, DeepSeek and Kimi-class models) on large GPU clusters, turn your findings into recipes and platform features that customers use, and present the results to the team and leadership. This is a 12-week, full-time, in-person internship. Candidates who want to see their research run in production, not just in a paper, will find it a good fit. What You'll Bring to the Team: Education: Currently enrolled in a PhD program in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Electrical Engineering or a related field, with an expected graduation date between Fall 2027 and Spring 2029. Research experience: 2+ years of research experience in machine learning or ML systems, including hands-on work with large language models: training or fine-tuning (SFT, RLHF, DPO, GRPO/PPO) or inference optimization. Programming: Strong Python and PyTorch; comfortable reading and modifying large ML codebases. Experimental rigor: You design controlled experiments, choose the right baselines and metrics, and can tell a real effect from noise. Systems awareness: Working knowledge of how LLM training and inference run on GPUs, such as batching, memory, mixed precision and parallelism. Communication: You explain complex results clearly in writing and in person, and you work well with engineers turning research into product. Bonus Points Publications at venues such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, MLSys, ACL, EMNLP or COLM on RL for LLMs, reward modeling, agents, efficient training or efficient inference. Hands-on experience with inference engines (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM) or training frameworks (verl, OpenRLHF, TRL, Megatron-LM, DeepSpeed). Experience with quantization, speculative decoding, GPU kernels (CUDA, Triton) or LoRA/PEFT methods. Experience building agent environments, tool-use sandboxes or evaluation harnesses. Open-source contributions to Training/Infernece libraries. description: About Parspec Founded in 2021, Parspec is revolutionizing the materials supply chain for the $13 trillion USD construction industry by digitizing and organizing the industry's product data. Our proprietary AI technology maintains a current and comprehensive catalogue of millions of products, enabling our customers to identify products that best meet their needs—instantly. Trusted by top designers, builders, distributors, manufacturers, and sales agents, and backed by leading venture investors, Parspec is paving the way for a more innovative, connected, and sustainable future in construction. Join us in building transformative technology that reshapes one of the world’s oldest and largest industries. The Opportunity How do you turn a successful first deployment into an enterprise-wide relationship? That question sits at the heart of this internship. We are looking for an intern to work alongside Parspec's sales leadership on one of the most important commercial questions we have: how do we build a repeatable expansion playbook for our largest customers? Our biggest accounts, national distributors and rep agencies, rarely start big. They begin with a single team, branch, or workflow. The ones that grow into enterprise relationships follow patterns we have only partially mapped. Your job is to find those patterns, turn them into account strategy, and prove that strategy on live deals. You will also help evaluate and structure partnerships with leading manufacturers, from the commercial economics to the deal terms. This is not a shadowing role. You will own a defined body of work with a concrete deliverable, present your findings directly to leadership, and watch your analysis get applied to active proposals while you are still here. If you see yourself heading toward go-to-market leadership, a startup operating role, or founding a company someday, this is a chance to learn enterprise growth by actually doing it, with real stakes. First-year MBA students will find the scope and the executive exposure especially well suited to a summer between years. What You Will Achieve and Key Responsibilities Find the growth pattern Analyze how our major distributor accounts expanded from their first deployment into additional workflows, branches, and business units Figure out what made the successful expansions work, and what stalled the ones that didn't, using product usage data, deal history, and conversations with sales leadership and customers Segment our installed base by expansion potential, separating accounts with real headroom from the ones that are already fully penetrated Help evaluate and structure partnerships with leading manufacturers, working through the commercial economics, the value exchange for both sides, an Build the account strategy Develop expansion plans for priority distributor and rep agency accounts, including sequencing, stakeholder mapping, and entry points for each new workflow Quantify what each additional workflow is worth, both for the customer (time saved, hit rate, revenue capture) and for Parspec (ARR, retention, account durability) Build the business case materials our sales leadership uses in executive-level customer conversations Put it into practice Apply your analysis to live expansion proposals during your internship, working directly with the CEO and sales leadership on deal strategy Help evaluate and structure partnerships with leading manufacturers, working through the commercial economics, the value exchange for both sides, an Deliver a documented expansion playbook covering account selection, value quantification, stakeholder strategy, and proposal templates that the sales team keeps running after your internship ends Present your findings and recommendations to Parspec's leadership team Why This Matters Parspec's growth increasingly depends not just on winning new logos but on deepening relationships with the customers who already trust us. Expansion revenue is the most capital-efficient growth a SaaS company has, and in a space as relationship-driven as construction distribution, the companies that systematize expansion win the category. Today, much of this knowledge lives in a few people's heads. This role turns it into a durable, repeatable system, and the playbook you build will outlast your internship. Who You Are You are a highly motivated student with strong analytical skills and genuine commercial instinct. You are just as comfortable in a spreadsheet as you are in a customer conversation. You form hypotheses quickly, test them against data, and communicate with the clarity that executive audiences expect. Ambiguity does not slow you down. You structure the problem, make the call, and adjust as you learn. Mandatory Qualifications Currently pursuing a degree (undergraduate or graduate) in Business, Economics, Management Science, Finance, Data Analytics, or a related field Strong analytical and modeling skills, including comfort building customer economics and business cases from incomplete data Structured problem-solving ability: you can break an ambiguous question down into an answerable workplan Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the presence to work directly with a CEO and customer-facing leaders A real ownership mentality: you have taken something from question to shipped result without being managed through it Preferred Experience First-year MBA students strongly preferred Prior professional experience in consulting, banking, revenue or business operations, enterprise sales, or a startup operating role Exposure to B2B SaaS business models, enterprise or key-account selling, or customer success economics Experience with CRM systems (e.g., HubSpot, Salesforce) and BI or analytics tools Interest in construction, building materials, industrial distribution, or vertical SaaS businesses Experience in fast-paced or early-stage startup environments What We Offer Direct, sustained working exposure to the CEO and senior sales leaders

description: Purpose in Every Position Pebl puts a world of talent at your fingertips. With our AI-powered Global Work Platform™, companies can hire, pay, and manage employees in 185+ countries—removing risk, red tape, and guesswork from global growth. Backed by more than a decade of compliance leadership and local expertise, Pebl helps businesses move fast, stay compliant, and scale with confidence. With Pebl, companies everywhere can hire great talent anywhere. Where Your Work Moves the Needle. At Pebl, every team member drives our success. Joining us means more than filling a role—you’re accountable for results and impact. Our values guide how we operate, execute, and collaborate across borders. By putting them into action, you’ll help us scale faster, compete harder, and lead the future of global work. What You'll Work On This role sits across three TechOps disciplines: infrastructure engineering, security engineering, and end-user support. You'll spend most of your time embedded with the DevOps and infrastructure team, learning how we build, monitor, and operate the platform that runs Pebl's global services. The remaining weeks rotate through InfoSec and IT Support, where you'll see how the same systems look from a security posture and from a frontline support angle. The goal isn't a surface-level taste of each team. It's to understand how they depend on each other. The firewall rule InfoSec sets today ends up as a support ticket when it blocks someone's tool tomorrow. The monitoring alert that wakes up an SRE on Saturday was probably triggered by a change an engineer made on Friday. By the end of the internship, you'll have worked on all three sides of that loop. This is a full-time-time, 12-week internship, with an expected start date no later than May 3rd, 2027. What You'll Own The specific work will shift based on what's live when you join, but across the three rotations expect a mix of: DevOps / SRE / Infrastructure (Weeks 1–8) Tracking down flaky CI/CD jobs in GitLab and improving build reliability for engineering teams Shadowing on-call rotations and working through real incidents: what broke, how we found it, how we fixed it, and what we changed so it doesn't happen again Writing Terraform to provision or modify AWS infrastructure and running it through our review and deploy process Building or improving Datadog dashboards and alerts for services that don't have enough visibility yet InfoSec (Weeks 9–10) Triaging open findings from security scanning tools and separating real risks from noise Reviewing access requests and understanding why we scope permissions to what people actually need Documenting a security control or process that currently lives only in someone's head IT Support (Weeks 11–12) Working the support queue directly: diagnosing hardware and software issues, escalating what needs escalating, and closing what you can resolve yourself Running employee onboarding or offboarding, which means touching identity providers, SaaS tooling, and hardware all in one workflow Writing a knowledge base article for a problem the team handles repeatedly but has never written down What We're Looking For Someone genuinely curious about how systems work and comfortable digging in when something breaks. More important than any specific tool is a willingness to ask questions until you actually understand something, then explain it back clearly to whoever needs to know. Specifically: Pursuing a degree in IT, Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or a related field Comfortable in the command line; Linux experience is a plus Some exposure to cloud concepts (AWS, GCP, or Azure) Strong written communication — a lot of this work is tickets, runbooks, and documentation Patient enough to follow a problem past the first answer Our Commitment to You At Pebl, we’re committed to supporting our team with comprehensive rewards and benefits designed to meet diverse needs across roles and locations. Health and Dental Insurance – Where applicable, to cover you and your loved ones. Retirement Savings + Employee Incentive Plan – Plan for the future while sharing our success. Please visit our career page for more information . Pebl is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We power global teams and believe diverse perspectives drive innovation and impact. Employment decisions at Pebl are based on qualifications, merit, and business needs. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, or gender identity), national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable law. We’re committed to fostering an inclusive culture where every teammate can thrive and do the best work of their career—anywhere in the world.

description: At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before. Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen. Role Overview Right now, Quality and Manufacturing at our Vineyard facility each keep their own calibration records for the measuring tools used to build and certify Seagliders. Tools could be used past their calibration due date without anyone catching it, and the measurement evidence behind our certification work is weaker than it should be. As we ramp up build volume next year, untangling divergent systems only gets harder, which is exactly why we want to get this right now, while the problem is still solvable from the ground up. As our Quality Intern , you'll take full ownership of designing and building that solution. You'll dig into engineering drawings to understand what level of precision each tool actually needs to protect, merge mismatched sets of records into a single trustworthy register and due-date schedule in ION, and spend real time on the shop floor talking with technicians to understand how tools are actually tracked and used day to day; this is critical. You'll be joining the Manufacturing & Supply Chain team at a moment when the systems you help build will directly shape how reliably we can scale production. If you're the kind of person who gets energized by turning scattered, high-stakes information into something clean, trustworthy, and lasting — and who wants real ownership of a project from first audit to final presentation — we'd love to have you on the team. What You'll Do Audit the Current State: You'll track down and catalog every measuring tool in use across Quality and Manufacturing, building a clear picture of what exists today and where the two teams' records diverge. Build the Unified Register: You'll merge two previously disconnected sets of calibration records into a single, standardized register in ION that both teams can rely on and maintain going forward. Define the Due-Date Schedule: Using engineering drawings and tolerance requirements, you'll determine which tools need calibrating, how often, and build the schedule that keeps everyone ahead of due dates. Get Hands-On With Technicians: You'll spend real time on the shop floor, talking directly with Quality and Manufacturing staff to understand how tools are actually used and tracked, not just how the paperwork says they should be. Catch What the Spreadsheets Miss: You'll dig into mismatched IDs, conflicting intervals, and missing due dates, making judgment calls about what belongs in the final system. Align Two Teams on One Process: You'll work with both Quality and Manufacturing to get everyone bought into a single shared process, rather than two teams quietly working around each other. Present Your Finished System: At the end of your term, you'll present the completed calibration register and schedule directly to Quality and Manufacturing leadership, along with documentation the team will keep using after you're gone. What You'll Bring Comfort With Engineering Drawings: You can read a drawing and understand tolerances well enough to reason about which tools need calibration and how tightly — not just copy an existing list. Sharp Spreadsheet Skills: You're accurate and efficient working across large sets of data, since merging two record systems and catching inconsistencies is fundamentally spreadsheet work. Meticulous Attention to Records: You understand that a wrong serial number or due date isn't a small mistake — it's the difference between a tool being trustworthy and a tool being used out of calibration unnoticed. Ease on the Shop Floor: You're comfortable walking up to technicians, asking questions, and helping two groups find common ground on how something should actually work. Hands-On Tool Experience: Any direct experience with measuring tools helps you recognize tool types quickly and understand what calibration is really protecting. Familiarity With Quality Standards: Exposure to ISO 9001 or ISO/IEC 17025 gives you a useful head start on what a compliant register needs to capture, like traceability and intervals. Basic Scripting a Plus: Some Python or SQL could help you automate comparisons between the two tool lists, though spreadsheets can get the job done too. Who We're Looking For Collaborative Team Player: You believe that great things happen when teams work together. You communicate effectively and collaborate with engineers, stakeholders, and other cross-functional teams to align on goals and move projects forward. You bring people together, ensuring that everyone is on the same page and moving towards a shared vision. Creative Problem Solver: You thrive on tackling complex challenges and finding innovative solutions. description: At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before. Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen. Role Overview REGENT's Paladin test program is where engineering development, vehicle maintenance, and on-water testing all converge, and this internship sits right at the center of it. You'll build and maintain the schedule that the entire program runs on, working directly with the vehicle and the test team rather than tracking progress from behind a desk. This is a DPM-style role in the truest sense: the milestone tracker isn't a document you update once a week, it's something you actively manage so that engineers, maintenance crews, and test leads are always working from the same plan. You'll join the Engineering & Technology Program Management team, a group that treats planning and tracking as real engineering work, not administrative overhead. Along the way, you'll be taught to see cost and schedule as engineering variables in their own right, a lens that's genuinely valuable whether you're headed toward program leadership or engineering management down the road. If you're someone who gets energized by being in the middle of the action, who sees a plan as something to steer rather than observe, and who wants hands-on exposure to how a real flight test program comes together, we'd love to have you on the team. What You'll Do Own the Master Schedule: You'll build and keep current the milestone tracker that ties together engineering, maintenance, and on-water testing for Paladin. This is a living document you actively manage, not something you dust off weekly. Get Hands-On with Paladin: You'll spend real time with the vehicle and the test team, not just behind a laptop. Being in the mix is how you'll understand what's actually happening on the ground, not just what's on paper. Support Vehicle Maintenance: You'll pitch in on maintenance work between test runs, giving you direct insight into what keeps Paladin flight-ready. That proximity to the vehicle is what makes your tracking actually useful. Know What Complete Really Means: You'll learn to distinguish between a part being ordered, installed, and tested, so your schedule reflects reality rather than optimism. That distinction is what keeps the whole program honest. Keep the Team Aligned: You'll make sure engineering, maintenance, and test ops are working from the same set of assumptions about what's next. When the plan stays current, the whole program moves faster together. Launch Your Own Initiatives: You'll take on program initiatives you can plan, manage, and see through to completion. By the end of your term, you'll be able to point to specific projects you drove start to finish. What You'll Bring Scheduling Tool Fluency: You're comfortable in Smartsheet, MS Project, Jira, or a similar tool. The specific platform matters less than being able to hit the ground organizing the program instead of learning software. Self-Directed Ownership: You can build and maintain a tracker across multiple workstreams without someone feeding you updates. You treat the plan as something to manage proactively, not react to. Mechanical Curiosity: Hands-on experience with engines, hulls, or mechanical systems, whether through marine, automotive, or other tinkering, gives you a head start here. A meaningful part of this role involves real vehicle maintenance support. Technical Grounding: You understand what an engineering or test milestone actually means when it's marked complete. That understanding is what keeps a schedule accurate instead of just looking fine on paper. Comfort Across Contexts: You're just as comfortable updating a tracker as you are standing next to the vehicle with the test team. You don't need the two worlds kept separate. Natural Organizational Instinct: You bring structure to dynamic, fast-moving work without slowing it down. You see a plan as something worth actively shaping. Who We're Looking For Collaborative Team Player: You believe that great things happen when teams work together. You communicate effectively and collaborate with engineers, stakeholders, and other cross-functional teams to align on goals and move projects forward. You bring people together, ensuring that everyone is on the same page and moving towards a shared vision. Creative Problem Solver: You thrive on tackling complex challenges and finding innovative solutions. Whether you're resolving installation challenges, debugging elusive electrical issues, or adapting on the fly during integration and test, you bring a practical, inventive mindset to every problem. You don't just patch issues - you improve processes, anticipate downstream impacts, and help turn one-off fixes into scalable solutions that raise the bar for future builds. Adaptable & Agile: In a fast-paced, ever-evolving startup environment, you quickly adapt to changing priorities and requirements. You approach challenges with a calm, resilient mindset, and know how to pivot and adjust your approach as needed, ensuring that progress continues without missing a beat. Innovative Mindset: You're driven by curiosity and a passion for technology. You're passionate about driving continuous improvement, embracing new technologies and methodologies to enhance efficiency,

description: Internship – Teleoperation & Data Labeling (m/f/d) – St. Gallen, Switzerland Who We Are We build the intelligence that lets robots sense, reason, and act in the real world—moving beyond the lab and into everyday industrial settings like warehouses and factories. Our technology closes the automation gaps that traditional systems can’t solve. We are on a mission to redefine how physical work gets done, and we’re looking for curious, bold thinkers to help shape the future of robotics with us. Overview We are looking for a tech-savvy intern with a passion for robotics, machine learning, or computer vision who wants hands-on experience in teleoperation and operating state-of-the-art robots. You will be based at one of our customer sites in St. Gallen, where our robots are running in live operations. We are growing our team in Switzerland: this position is employed directly through our Swiss entity based in Zurich. This role is perfect for someone eager to learn, contribute, and gain practical exposure to advanced AI-driven robotic systems. Your Responsibilities • Robot Teleoperation: Collect high-quality data by controlling robots through a VR headset. • Data Labeling: Label visual data (images, point clouds) with speed and precision. • Use terminal basics to run existing tooling (bash + Python scripts) for data collection, uploads, and checks • Do simple debugging: reproduce issues, collect logs, and write clear problem reports (steps, expected vs actual, timestamps, logs/screenshots) • Collaboration: Work with a fast-paced, innovative tech team, both on site at our customer and remotely with our engineering team. • Travel to other sites within Switzerland or the EU may occasionally be required Your Qualifications • You pay close attention to detail and enjoy precise, careful work • You’re comfortable with computers and curious about tech. Some experience with the command line or Python is a plus, but we’ll teach you what you need • You stay calm and focused in a fast-moving team • You’re open to occasional travel • You are eligible to work in Switzerland (Swiss or EU/EFTA citizenship, or a valid Swiss work permit) • Nice to have: a driving license valid in Switzerland Location • Work location: St. Gallen, Switzerland, on site at our customer, with occasional travel within Switzerland or the EU • Employment through our Swiss entity in Zurich Duration: Minimum 3 months, full-time (40 h/week) Our Interview Plan 1. Application 2. Take-home assignment: You’ll complete a short, role-relevant task with clear instructions and a deadline. 3. Cultural fit interview (40 min): A conversation about how you work, what motivates you, and what you’re looking for. Expect CV highlights, your “why,” and time for your questions. 4. On-site assessment day: Meet the team and collaborate on a real challenge similar to the work you’d do here. You’ll get a clear feel for the environment, ways of working, and the role. What We Offer • Real-world experience with cutting-edge robotic systems. • Regular team events and a supportive team culture. • An opportunity to develop hands-on skills in a high-growth robotics company. How to apply: Please apply via this posting or send your application to janine.schoenenberg@sereact.ai Note to applicants: We are currently experiencing a high volume of interest in this role. Due to this, our review process is taking a bit longer than usual. We appreciate your patience.

description: About Us Socket helps devs and security teams ship faster by cutting out security busywork. Thousands of orgs use Socket to safely find, audit, and manage open source code. Our customers - from Anthropic to xAI, and Figma to Vercel - love Socket (just check out their tweets to see for yourself!) Founded by Feross Aboukhadijeh , a long-time open source maintainer with software downloaded over a billion times a month, Socket has raised $ 125M in funding from top angels, operators, and security leaders. About the Role You will collaborate with world-class researchers and software engineers to conduct research on the emerging threats against software supply chain. This internship offers a unique opportunity to translate cutting-edge research ideas into real-world systems that safeguard millions of developers worldwide. You will contribute to the design and implementation of large-scale data collection and analysis pipelines, conduct in-depth investigations of malicious activity in open source ecosystems, and prototype novel techniques for detecting fraud and abuse on platforms such as GitHub. We are interested in research on any aspect of software supply chain security. As one of our research interns, you will not only push the boundaries of software supply chain security but also help shape the culture and direction of a fast-growing security company. This role is ideal for PhD students eager to bridge academia and industry and bring innovative research into production environments while gaining hands-on development experience in a high-impact, mission-driven setting. You can read more about Socket Labs here . What You'll Do Conduct applied research on emerging threats in the software supply chain (e.g., self-propagating malware in package ecosystems, dependency hallucinations, AI emerging threats) and translate findings into detection prototypes and publish the results. Design and evaluate novel algorithms for identifying malicious or inauthentic activity across ecosystems such as npm, PyPI, and GitHub. Leverage data science and machine learning techniques to model suspicious publishing behaviors, coordinated activity, and fraud campaigns. Develop automated research tools to collect, transform, and analyze large-scale datasets from third-party APIs (e.g., npm, GitHub, PyPI). Prototype and validate detection systems that can be integrated into Socket’s threat intelligence platform, bridging research insights with production impact. Collaborate with engineers and designers to experiment with new ways of surfacing research findings in user-facing interfaces and developer workflows. Publish research outputs internally (dashboards, reports, proofs-of-concept) to influence product strategy and publish papers in conferences/share with the broader research community. Contribute to the early team culture, bringing a research-driven perspective to technical discussions, prioritization, and the company’s long-term vision. What You'll Bring You must be enrolled in a PhD program in computer science (or related field) and eager to apply your research expertise to real-world problems in software supply chain security. Strong background in one or more of the following research areas: software supply chain security, program analysis, or AI security. Proficiency with languages commonly used for prototyping and research (e.g., JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, or similar). Familiarity with software and systems security concepts, such as threat modeling, malware analysis, or adversarial behavior in open ecosystems. Experience conducting research involving data analysis, statistical methods, and experimental evaluation. Strong analytical and creative problem-solving skills; able to explore novel approaches and rigorously evaluate their effectiveness. Self-motivated and comfortable driving independent research while collaborating with an interdisciplinary team. Strong written and verbal communication skills for presenting research findings and collaborating across engineering and design. Experience with publishing research at top-tier academic conferences, like IEEE S&P, USENIX Security, CCS, and NDSS. Prior work in one or more of the following is a plus: Static/dynamic analysis of software or binaries Open source security research Experience with Socket-supported ecosystems Vulnerability discovery Building scalable data pipelines or visualization dashboards Hiring is a big decision on both sides. Read more about our Hiring Philosophy and how we approach the process at Socket. Benefits: Our benefits are crafted to support you and your family, so you can take care of what matters most and thrive in and outside of work. We offer: Market competitive salary bands Meaningful equity program Comprehensive health benefits for you and your family (99% coverage) Flexible time-off, holidays, and winter shutdown to rest & recharge Paid parental leave Remote-first, with quarterly team off-sites At Socket, we Pursue Excellence: We set ourselves apart by consistently delivering work of exceptional quality and distinction. Move with urgency and focus: We prioritize swift, decisive action. Think rigorously: We care about being right and it often takes reasoning from first principles to get there. We value alternative perspectives and have constructive discussions. Trust and amplify: We overtrust, always assume good intent, and give specific feedback to help each other improve. Feel a strong sense of ownership: We wear many hats and feel a strong sense of overall ownership of the company and we're non-territorial regarding our nominal domains. Are customer obsessed: We relentlessly prioritize the needs of our customers, striving to exceed their expectations and delight them at every interaction.

description:
Work Arrangement

This is an onsite position.

Job Overview

The Naval Architecture Intern supports vessel design, analysis, modeling, and engineering activities across a diverse portfolio of maritime programs. Working under the guidance of experienced naval architects and marine engineers, this position provides hands-on exposure to vessel design, hydrostatics, hydrodynamics, stability, structures, and marine operations while contributing to real-world engineering projects.

 

Essential Functions

  • Assist with vessel design studies, concept development activities, and engineering analyses.
  • Support hydrostatic, stability, resistance and powering, seakeeping, and vessel performance evaluations.
  • Develop and modify vessel arrangements, engineering drawings, and 3D models under engineering supervision.
  • Assist in preparing technical reports, calculations, engineering documentation, presentations, and design packages.
  • Support evaluation of vessel layouts, compartment arrangements, mission payload integration, and equipment installations.
  • Assist with structural assessments and engineering analyses using established naval architecture methods and tools.
  • Support application of classification society, customer, and regulatory requirements to vessel designs.
  • Participate in design reviews, engineering discussions, and multidisciplinary project meetings.
  • Collect, organize, and analyze engineering data from vessels, simulations, models, tests, and field activities.
  • Support dockside inspections, vessel surveys, sea trials, testing, and verification activities as assigned.
  • Document engineering observations, findings, lessons learned, and technical recommendations.
  • Collaborate with naval architecture, mechanical, electrical, systems, software, and production personnel on engineering tasks.
  • Learn and apply company engineering processes, configuration management practices, documentation standards, and technical procedures.
  • Perform other duties as assigned in support of engineering and maritime operations.

Standard Essential Functions

  • Regular and reliable attendance on a full time basis [or in accordance with posted schedule].
  • Responsible for exhibiting professional behavior with both internal and external business associates that reflects positively on the company and is consistent with the company's policies and practices.
  • Embodies AEVEX’s cultural values and aligns daily actions with department goals and company culture.

 

Qualifications            

  • Fundamental understanding of naval architecture and marine engineering principles.
  • Coursework exposure to hydrostatics, hydrodynamics, fluid mechanics, statics, dynamics, or related engineering disciplines.
  • Familiarity with vessel stability, resistance and powering, seakeeping, structures, arrangements, or marine systems.
  • Basic understanding of engineering drawing interpretation and technical documentation practices.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and critical-thinking skills.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to document technical work clearly and effectively.
  • Ability to learn new engineering tools, methods, and processes.
  • Ability to receive technical guidance and incorporate feedback from experienced engineers.
  • Ability to work both independently and as part of a multidisciplinary engineering team.

Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. The community you will join:

Airbnb is excited to welcome Software Engineering Interns for our 2027 Summer Intern Program from May 24, 2027 - August 13, 2027.

At Airbnb, we believe technology has the power to bring people together — and our engineers are the ones building it. Our Engineering org is a diverse, fast-moving group of teams working across Payments, Trust, Marketing, Relevance & Personalization, and more. Together, we're tackling some of the hardest problems in tech: search relevance at global scale, fraud prevention, seamless payments, and fueling growth — all while delivering a product experience that feels effortless and beautiful. About AppLovin

AppLovin makes technologies that help businesses of every size connect to their ideal customers. The company provides end-to-end advertising solutions for businesses to reach, monetize and grow their global audiences. For more information about AppLovin, visit: www.applovin.com.

To deliver on this mission, our global team is composed of team members with life experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives that mirror our developers and customers around the world. At AppLovin, we are intentional about the team and culture we are building, seeking candidates who are outstanding in their own right and also demonstrate their support of others.

About Gist

Gist is a new consumer social app built by AppLovin, a handbook for the curious. We’re building a lifestyle platform for adults 25–45 around the relatable, actionable content people use to navigate their daily lives: food, wellness, fashion, family, and personal finance. We’re building our creator ecosystem from the ground up, and we’re looking for an intern to help us find the talent that will define it.

The best outcome of this internship is seeing the partnerships you build contribute to Gist’s growth.


About the Role

This is a research and pipeline role sitting at the center of our platform partnerships team. You won’t be filing decks or sitting in on calls. You’ll be doing the ground-level work that makes creator partnership recruitment possible: finding the right talent, agency, growth platforms, tracking outreach, and keeping our partnership database sharp and current.


A Day in the Life

  • Research and identify potential partners across creators, brands, agencies, and communities that can help grow Gist
  • Support partner outreach by drafting communications, coordinating follow-ups, and tracking responses
  • Maintain our partnership pipeline, keeping contacts, opportunities, status, and next steps organized and up to date
  • Evaluate potential partners based on audience fit, strategic relevance, and growth potential
  • Surface emerging trends and partnership opportunities that could strengthen Gist’s content, community, and reach
  • Build and automate workflows using AI tools to improve research, outreach, and pipeline management
  • Track and report on partnership performance using data and KPIs to measure impact on Gist’s growth

 

Who You Are

  • Bachelor’s degree or above in Science, Computer Science, Business or any related fields graduating December 2027 or Spring 2028
  • Strong AI skills and genuine interest in building automation workflows
  • Comfortable with data: you think in metrics, track what you do, and can connect your work to measurable outcomes
  • A clear, confident communicator who adapts quickly and is receptive to feedback
  • Curious about how platform partnerships work: the deal structures, the pitch, the relationship-building
  • Sharp, flexible thinker who can pivot quickly as priorities shift
  • Prior experience in influencer marketing, talent management, or creator-focused roles is a plus


Why Join

  • A front-row seat to how a well-funded platform builds its creator ecosystem from zero
  • Direct exposure to the full creator partnership lifecycle: sourcing, outreach, negotiation, and onboarding
  • Mentorship from a senior creator partnerships team with deep roots in talent agencies and management
  • Real, meaningful work from day one: the creators you find could end up shaping what Gist becomes
  • Opportunity for full-time conversion for exceptional performers

description:
What we’re building

The marine industry supports recreation, global commerce, and national defense. And yet it runs on technology that hasn't meaningfully changed in fifty years. Until now.

Arc is on a mission to electrify the marine industry. We're rethinking powertrains, software, and vessel designs from first principles. And we're already executing. We started with consumers to develop and harden our core technology. We’re now scaling production of our flagship model with new models and sectors on the horizon. Now we’re extending our platform to commercial applications, starting with tugs, ferries, and defense, with years worth of signed contracts and a pipeline that spans every vessel type on the water.

The technology is proven, the momentum is building, and the opportunity is enormous. The marine industry is going electric and Arc is building the platform that powers it

Who we’re looking for

We’re looking for a hands-on, curious engineering student who wants to understand why things fail in the field and how to fix them for good. We pride ourselves on transparency and operate in a lean, high-trust environment that encourages everyone to take ownership over their domain.

You will be a full-time member of our Service team, will report directly to our service engineer and will work from our manufacturing facility in Los Angeles. Given that we’re a startup, you will be working in a fast-moving, dynamic environment that requires adaptability. That said, here are some responsibilities and qualifications we expect to stay relatively constant for this role.

What You'll Do

  • Developing and documenting standard repair processes, work instructions, and troubleshooting guides for common field issues
  • Diagnosing field failures alongside Service and Vehicle Engineers, using boat data, logs, photos, and teardowns to find root causes
  • Structuring field failure data into a consistent format (failure mode, system, part, root cause, corrective action)
  • Reporting failure trends and recurring issues to engineering, manufacturing, and quality teams to support our quality initiative
  • Following up on corrective actions and refining repair procedures based on technician and engineer feedback

Minimum Qualifications

  • Currently pursuing a degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Mechatronics, Manufacturing, or a related engineering field
  • Comfortable with hands-on work around hardware, tools, and vehicles
  • Strong organization and attention to detail when structuring data and writing documentation
  • Proficiency in Excel or Google Sheets (pivot tables, charts, basic formulas)

Bonus Qualifications

  • Experience on a student engineering team (Formula SAE, Baja, solar car, robotics) or in a repair shop
  • Familiarity with root cause methods such as 5 Whys, 8D, FMEA, or Pareto analysis
  • Exposure to diagnostic tools (multimeter, CAN tools) or reading wiring diagrams; experience with Python, SQL, or BI tools
  • Comfortable pushing a fast but sustainable pace
  • Enthusiasm for boating and clean energy

At Arc, we encourage diversity and consider all qualified applicants equally for employment, regardless of background, identity, or status. You’re always welcome to reach out even if you don’t meet many of these qualifications. Passion and aptitude make up for a lot.

What we offer

The base pay for this role is $36 per hour. 

Additionally, as an Arc Intern, you'll also get:

  • Boat days – Yes, we actually go out on the water. A lot.
  • Retirement savings — Traditional and Roth 401(k) access
  • Safety support — Reimbursement for PPE, ergonomic equipment, and anything that ensures we keep our crew safe
  • Relocation Assistance
  • Mentorship Opportunities
  • Office perks — Daily lunches, snacks, and good coffee while onsite

Our values

We move with urgency and build with care. We value these five things above all else:

  • Ownership over both your work and the company’s success
  • Empathy for colleagues and for customers
  • Humility in problem solving and collaboration
  • Pragmatism for navigating ambiguity quickly and sensibly 
  • Inclusion of different backgrounds, opinions, cultures, and perspectives.

We want people who share and embody these values. It is vital that our values align - we’d be happy to elaborate on any or all of these during the interview process.

About us

At Auctane, we are united by a passion to help businesses deliver — whatever their size, wherever they are, and however they operate. We make it possible for businesses to meet the ever-changing requirements of their industry and customer expectations. Auctane products enable hundreds of thousands of businesses to annually mail and ship billions of items — over $200 billion worth — to recipients around the globe.

The Auctane family of mailing and shipping software products includes ShipStation, Stamps.com, ShipStation API, Metapack, GlobalPost, and Packlink. Our partners include Amazon, UPS, USPS, eBay, BigCommerce, Shopify, WooCommerce, and Walmart.

Our values

Make it Right. Play to Win. Win as One

 

About the team

Vipers is an engineering team within ShipStation Global, part of the Auctane family of shipping and e-commerce brands. We build and run financial and post-shipment products for ShipStation customers – from automated reconciliation of carrier shipping invoices against contracted rates, which surfaces billing discrepancies and overcharges, to solutions that protect merchants’ parcels against loss and damage in transit. We are a small, cross-functional team of engineers who own our products end to end: from design and development, through testing and deployment, to production support. We value pragmatic engineering, ownership, collaboration and continuous learning.

About the role

We are looking for a motivated student to join the Vipers team as an Associate Software Engineer in a paid internship role, initially planned for 6 months. Over recent months the team has taken on two business-critical initiatives in the shipping protection and carrier invoice reconciliation areas, and we need additional capacity to deliver them with high quality. As the team does not have a dedicated QA function, a key focus of this role will be building and maintaining automated end-to-end (E2E) test coverage for our invoice reconciliation product, reducing the risk of defects reaching our customers. You will work side by side with experienced engineers, receive hands-on mentorship, and gradually take on development tasks across our .NET backend and React frontend. This is a great opportunity to start your software engineering career on real, production products in an international environment.
This is an internship position with a hybrid setup (2 days per week in office) and is located in Wrocław, Poland. The compensation will range from 35 to 38 PLN/ hour.

What will you be doing?

  • Design, write and maintain automated E2E tests (Playwright, TypeScript) for our invoice reconciliation web application. 
  • Work with engineers and the product owner to identify critical user flows and turn them into test scenarios and acceptance criteria. 
  • Integrate automated tests into CI pipelines and help keep them fast, stable and reliable.

You will map how work gets done today, measure a baseline, build and pilot two working tools, and hand off a repeatable process the People team keeps using. You will partner with HR Business Partners, People Operations specialists, and managers, and present your results to People and business leadership in August.

Program Details
Our summer program will be 10-12 weeks from mid-May - August 2027 with the expectation of being in the office 3-4 days per week, as determined by the sponsor. Compensation will be set at an hourly rate of $35-40 per hour. Top performing associates may have the opportunity to be considered for full-time roles at DriveWealth at the conclusion of the program, based on performance and team needs. Must have an expected graduation date from December 2027 to December 2028.

What You’ll Do

Process Mapping and Baseline 

  • Document how common HR workflows and employee lifecycle tasks are handled today, and identify the biggest pain points and opportunities for automation and AI assistance.
  • For each opportunity, establish a baseline and agree on a target with your sponsor, so we can tell whether what you build worked.
  • Identify high-impact opportunities for HR optimization (we expect about two, but the number and type are driven by what you find).

Build AI Solutions

  • Build working solutions for the People team that combine LLMs, APIs, and automation frameworks. Solutions might be AI assistants, automated workflows, dashboards, etc.
    • Focus areas may include: Onboarding/Offboarding, HR Helpdesk & Knowledge Base, Employee Lifecycle documentation (offer letters, onboarding communications, role change letters)
  • Run a small pilot and measure results against your baseline.

  • Document what you build, including prompts, workflows, and a short playbook, so the team can maintain and extend it without you.
  • Use only approved AI tools, and keep personal or confidential information out of tools that are not approved.
  • Check for accuracy, tone, and correctness, and keep a list of topics the tools should not engage with (policy, pay, benefits, etc.)

What You’ll Need

  • Current undergraduate or graduate student in Human Resources, Psychology, Machine Learning, Data Science, Data Analytics, or a Related Field.
  • Hands-on experience using AI tools (such as LLMs Claude, ChatGPT or automation tools) on a real project, which you should be ready to describe in your application.

  • Sound judgment and discretion with confidential employee information.
  • Comfort working with HR partners, managers, and business leaders, and curiosity about how people, culture, and technology come together at a fast-growing fintech.

Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. DriveWealth is unable to sponsor an employment Visa at this time.

Quantitative Research Intern – Systematic FICC - Hong Kong

About the Team

The Systematic Rates team researches and runs fully systematic, data-driven strategies in global interest FICC markets. We combine solid statistics, careful engineering and a good feel for how markets work to build and improve systematic trading strategies.

The Role

You'll work closely with the portfolio manager. You'll do hands-on research and development across the whole strategy process, and you'll own real projects with real impact, not side tasks.

Responsibilities

  • Research, prototype and backtest systematic strategies across FICC products such as swaps and foreign exchange.
  • Build and maintain production pipelines, research tools and analytics libraries.
  • Run statistical analysis on market data: signal research, factor analysis, regime analysis, and transaction cost and capacity studies.
  • Help monitor and analyse the performance and risk of live strategies.
  • Write clean, tested, well-documented code that the team can rely on and reuse.

Requirements

  • Strong coding skills. You're proficient in Python (or a similar language). You can design, write, debug and explain your own code. We expect real engineering ability, not just prompting AI tools for code you can't reason about.
  • Strong math and statistics. You're comfortable with probability, linear algebra, regression and time-series analysis.
  • Basic knowledge of financial instruments. You understand FICC market at a foundational level, and you're keen to learn more.

Nice to Have

  • Experience on a fixed income or rates desk (trading, research or strategy). This is a plus, not a requirement.
  • Experience with pandas, NumPy, SciPy, statsmodels or similar, plus SQL and version control (Git).
  • Experience with backtesting frameworks, or with large and messy financial datasets.

Availability

  • Start date is as soon as possible.
  • Full-time placement preferred for a season (e.g., an off-cycle).
  • Duration will be 3 - 6 months in our Hong Kong office
  • Part-time candidates can be considered who can commit to at least 4 days a week.
