Work Period: January 2027 to June 2027. This is a full - time, 40 hours per week position with 5 days in office.

About Pioneering Medicines

Pioneering Medicines, Flagship Pioneering’s in-house drug development unit, is dedicated to conceiving and developing a broad portfolio of life-changing treatments for patients built from Flagship’s innovative platforms. Harnessing the drug development expertise of its team together with the power of Flagship’s multiple scientific platforms, Pioneering Medicines explores and identifies new product concepts which are then advanced jointly with Flagship’s bioplatform companies. Within Flagship’s Innovation Supply Chain partnerships, Pioneering Medicines works with external collaborators to apply its unique approach to partners’ R&D priorities. These partnerships are highly co-creative strategic alliances that accelerate therapeutic innovation by bringing together partners spanning the full spectrum of drug discovery, development, and production.

About Flagship Pioneering

Pioneering Medicines was founded by Flagship Pioneering's venture creation engine that invents and builds platform companies, each with the potential for multiple products that transform human health or sustainability. Since its launch in 2000, Flagship has originated and fostered more than 100 scientific ventures, resulting in more than $90 billion in aggregate value. Many of the company’s Flagship has founded have addressed humanity’s most urgent challenges: vaccinating billions of people against COVID-19, curing intractable diseases, improving human health, preempting illness, and feeding the world by improving the resiliency and sustainability of agriculture. Flagship has been recognized twice on FORTUNE’s “Change the World” list, an annual ranking of companies that have made a positive social and environmental impact through activities that are part of their core business strategies and has been twice named to Fast Company’s annual list of the World’s Most Innovative Companies. Learn more about Flagship at www.flagshippioneering.com.

Flagship Pioneering Co-Op Program

Welcome to Flagship Pioneering Co-Op Program for the cohort dreaming big and taking courageous leaps. You'll join fellow peers across our ecosystem of companies and learning firsthand how we build first-in-category companies. You’ll have access to enrichment sessions, a dedicated professional development track, and a mentor that help guide you toward your next step. By the end, you will carry on a meaningful project outcome, a genuine network, and a front-row view of how Flagship pioneer new ventures that change the world.

Position Description 

We are seeking a motivated Drug Substance Co-Op with a chemical, biochemical, or biomedical engineering background and hands-on skill in in silico modeling of unit operations. This role will support Drug Substance process development in the CMC and Bioprocess Development group, using mechanistic and data-driven models to guide process design, scale-up, and tech transfer for biologics, small molecules, and peptides.

Reporting to a Drug Substance process development lead, the co-op will work alongside upstream, downstream, analytical, and regulatory CMC colleagues and gain exposure to our network of CDMO partners. The co-op is a chance to apply engineering fundamentals to live programs and see how modeling decisions shape real manufacturing processes.

The co-op is expected to run >6 mo. or part-time during the academic year, with a defined project and an end-of-term presentation to the CMC team.

Key Responsibilities

In Silico Unit Operation Modeling

  • Build, calibrate, and run models of drug substance unit operations (for example, cell culture and fermentation, chromatography, ultrafiltration/diafiltration, viral inactivation and filtration, crystallization, and peptide synthesis and purification) using mechanistic, hybrid, or statistical approaches.
  • Use models to evaluate operating ranges, identify sensitive process parameters, and compare scale-up and scale-down options.
  • Run sensitivity analyses and simulation-based studies to support process characterization and design-space thinking.

Data Analysis & Process Understanding

  • Collect, clean, and analyze lab, pilot, and CDMO batch data to fit and verify models.
  • Apply statistical tools and design of experiments (DoE) to plan and interpret studies.
  • Summarize model results, assumptions, and limitations in clear technical reports and presentations.

Tech Transfer & CDMO Support

  • Support tech transfer by translating model outputs into process descriptions, parameter ranges, and risk assessments for CDMO partners.
  • Help review batch records and process data from external manufacturing sites and flag deviations from model predictions.

About the Role:

As an Economics Research Intern on the Gusto Insights team, you’ll help us turn Gusto’s platform data into research on the small business economy, including hiring, pay, entrepreneurship, and the future of work. Insights publishes widely cited public research, including the monthly Small Business Jobs Report. The ideal candidate is a technically strong, curious economist who can turn messy data into a clear story and is passionate about helping small businesses thrive.

You’ll own at least one well-scoped, high-visibility project from our research roadmap and data-infrastructure backlog, taking it from raw data through analysis to a shipped deliverable. You’ll work with mentorship from an established team and partner with colleagues across Communications, Marketing, and Data. You’ll also use AI-assisted practices to accelerate your analysis and extend the reach of our research. The internship runs ~10–12 weeks in summer 2027.

This is a San Francisco-based role with expectations to be in office 2 days per week.

Here’s what you’ll do day-to-day:

  • Own a Project End-to-End: Take a self-contained project from raw data through analysis to a finished, public-ready deliverable.
  • Analytical Depth: Analyze large-scale, messy administrative data using Python and SQL. Apply econometric methods, including causal inference and regression modeling, to separate signal from noise and make defensible claims.
  • Build and Leverage AI: Use Claude Code and other agentic tools in your daily workflow for exploration, code, and drafting. Verify their output with a critical eye.
  • Communication: Turn analysis into clear charts and a crisp narrative for non-technical audiences. Our output is public-facing.
  • Collaboration: Work with cross-functional partners to scope your project, get feedback, and deliver insights that matter.
  • Economic Measurement: Sharpen the indicators we publish every month. You might build more detailed cuts of the Small Business Jobs Report by industry, region, and company size, test whether Gusto data can predict BLS revisions, or define and validate a new economic metric from scratch.
  • Data Infrastructure: Strengthen the foundation our research runs on. Turn one-off scripts into reproducible, documented pipelines, help move core workflows to modern tools like dbt, and bring new datasets into our research environment so the team can answer questions it can’t today.
  • Data Products & AI Interfaces: Build tools that put our research in more people’s hands. This could mean expanding our public economic data page, creating interactive visualizations, or extending the AI agents and research assistants that let reporters, partners, and colleagues explore Gusto’s data and findings on their own.
  • Present: Share your findings with the Insights team and partners at the end of the internship.

  • Currently enrolled in a four year degree or master’s program with an expected graduation date of December 2027 or May 2028.   • Demonstrated fluency with LLMs and agentic coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, or similar), and good judgment about when to verify their output.

description:
Heartflow is a medical technology company advancing the diagnosis and management of coronary artery disease, the #1 cause of death worldwide, using cutting-edge technology. The flagship product—an AI-driven, non-invasive cardiac test supported by the ACC/AHA Chest Pain Guidelines called the Heartflow FFRCT Analysis—provides a color-coded, 3D model of a patient’s coronary arteries indicating the impact blockages have on blood flow to the heart. Heartflow is the first AI-driven non-invasive integrated heart care solution across the CCTA pathway that helps clinicians identify stenoses in the coronary arteries (RoadMap™Analysis), assess coronary blood flow (FFRCT Analysis), and characterize and quantify coronary atherosclerosis (Plaque Analysis). Our pipeline of products is growing and so is our team; join us in helping to revolutionize precision heartcare.

Heartflow is a publicly traded company (HTFL) that has received international recognition for exceptional strides in healthcare innovation, is supported by medical societies around the world, cleared for use in the US, UK, Europe, Japan and Canada, and has been used for more than 750,000 patients worldwide.

We are seeking a highly motivated Platform Engineering Intern to join our team in-person at our San Francisco office for the Summer 2027 term.   • Container Orchestration: Work with modern containerization technologies to deploy and manage microservices effectively.
  • Developer Tooling: Identify bottlenecks and improve internal developer tools to enhance engineering productivity across the organization.

  • Technical Curiosity: Familiarity with or a strong desire to learn Infrastructure as Code, CI/CD practices, Linux systems, and container orchestration (e.g., Docker, Kubernetes).

  • Document the tools you build and present results to the team, so the team keeps using them after the internship.

  • Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's program in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering or a related field
  • Interest in hardware systems engineering: PCB design, board bring-up and system test

description:
Power Electronics Test Intern

Lunar Energy builds home energy products that make clean power abundant and accessible: inverters, batteries, and the software that ties them together. As a Power Electronics Test Intern, you will test those products, from the first bench measurement to the certification report. Your work covers two jobs that usually sit apart: power electronics performance testing, and compliance testing for safety, grid interconnection, and electromagnetic compatibility (EMC). You will work on inverters, batteries, energy storage systems, and electric vehicle supply equipment (EVSE, or EV chargers), in our high-voltage lab, alongside design, firmware, reliability, and manufacturing engineers. What you find will change what we ship.

What you will gain: Gain practical experience in designing and testing Lunar’s products, while developing a comprehensive understanding of the full lifecycle from design to validation and certification. You will collaborate closely with design engineers, observe how testing data directly informs engineering decisions, and deliver key insights derived from test results and rigorous data analysis.

Lunar Energy was founded to transition homes to 100% clean energy—making our electricity greener, our air cleaner and our energy more safe, secure and reliable for all. We’re a fast-growing, global company building the world’s best clean energy products to electrify all homes and connect communities to form clean, resilient virtual power plants.

On a given day at Lunar, you’ll likely…

  • Test inverters, batteries, energy storage systems, and EVSE for efficiency, power quality, protection response, fault behavior, transients, and thermal performance
  • Run compliance and pre-compliance tests against safety, grid interconnection, and EMC standards, and help prepare products for testing for  certification.
  • Work with Compliance Engineers, & write test plans and procedures that trace each test back to a clause in the standard it supports.
  • Build and run test setups with grid simulators, programmable AC and DC sources, battery cyclers, electronic loads, power analyzers, oscilloscopes, EV simulators, and environmental chambers.
  • Automate test sequences and data processing in Python so a test that takes a day by hand takes an hour.
  • Design targeted experiments to isolate failure modes, then diagnose them and drive root cause analysis with corrective and preventive actions.
  • Analyze test data, report findings clearly, and bring early compliance risks to design reviews before they become redesigns. Review engineering changes for their effect on existing certifications
  • Keep detailed records of tests, analyses, and corrective actions, and prepare test reports and technical files for internal teams and outside certification bodies.
  • Work with design, firmware, reliability, and manufacturing engineers to protect design integrity and inform design decisions.

 

Desired Skills:

Required

  • Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD in Electrical Engineering or a closely related field (Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Aerospace Engineering, or Physics) or recently graduated.
  • Strong grasp of electrical engineering fundamentals: AC power, three-phase systems, power converters (AC/DC, DC/DC, DC/AC), and basic control and protection concepts.
  • Hands-on lab experience with oscilloscopes, power supplies, multimeters, and current and voltage probes.
  • Experience with Python, C, or C++, and with processing and plotting measurement data.
  • Strong debugging instincts: you can isolate a failure mode, design an experiment, and close a finding with a documented root cause.
  • Careful, safety-minded work habits, with the discipline that high-voltage lab work demands.
  • Clear written and verbal communication, including explaining a technical result to both engineers and non-engineers.
  • Comfort with ambiguity, a fast pace, and working across teams and with outside labs. 
  • An ownership mindset: you follow a problem through to the end

Preferred

  • Coursework or project experience in power electronics, grid-connected inverters, battery systems, or EV charging
  • Familiarity with safety and grid standards for energy products, such as UL 1741, IEEE 1547, UL 1973, UL 9540
  • Familiarity with EMC testing and standards, such as FCC Part 15, and IEC 61000: conducted and radiated emissions, electrostatic discharge, electrical fast transient, and surge immunity
  • Experience with automated test systems, such as instrument control with SCPI, PyVISA.
  • Experience with battery testing (cycling, thermal chambers) or with reliability, abuse, or environmental stress testing.
  • Data analysis and visualization experience in Python.
  • Prior lab research in power electronics, energy storage, or high-voltage systems
  • Comfort using AI tools to speed up analysis and documentation, with the judgment to check their output and protect confidential data.

Join Method as part of our 2027 Summer Residency Program as a Product Management Resident and help build, ship, and learn as part of a small cross-functional team of Product, Design, and Engineering Residents.

Method is a strategic design and product development consultancy with 25 years of experience, and a GlobalLogic company within the Hitachi family. This residency is a hands-on way to see how a global digital consultancy works from the inside: you will discover user needs, define solutions, and drive development alongside the people who do this for clients every day.

Product management is changing quickly as AI takes on more of the research, synthesis, specification, and reporting work. We built this residency for people who want to learn the craft as it is being rewritten, not as it was practiced five years ago.

The role: Product Management for the AI era

The modern Product Manager is less a document producer and more a decision-maker who directs, checks and refines work done with AI. At Method we describe this as AI-native product management: you still own the "why" and the "what," but you use AI to move from research to a testable idea in days rather than weeks, and you apply judgment to what it produces.

As a Resident, you will practice the skills that set an AI-native PM apart:

  • Framing the problem well. Writing clear specs and giving AI the right context, so the output is useful the first time.
  • Working with AI as a teammate. Using AI for research synthesis, prototyping and drafting, and knowing which tasks to delegate and which to keep.
  • Verifying, not trusting. Checking AI-generated work for accuracy, bias and fit with real user needs before it reaches a decision.
  • Knowing where AI belongs. Judging where AI creates value for a user or business, and saying plainly where it will not pay off.
  • Leading people through change. Helping teams adopt new tools and ways of working so they actually stick.

Because the work now spans more disciplines, the strongest PMs are increasingly hybrids. Method staffs and develops people in blended roles for exactly this reason.

Choose your hybrid lens

Every Resident learns the core product craft. Beyond that, you will lean into one of two hybrid paths, shaped by your interests and the product your team is building.

Product Strategy / Design Hybrid

A product strategist with design fluency, who shapes a proposition and proves it through design artifacts rather than long documents.

  • Turn research and stakeholder input into a clear product concept, then express it as journey maps, flows and clickable prototypes.
  • Use AI to go from interviews to a testable prototype quickly, and bring the craft and judgment to know when the result is good enough to put in front of users.
  • Work side by side with Design Residents on usability testing, and let what users do, not what a deck says, drive the next decision.

A good fit if you are curious about users, like making ideas tangible, and enjoy workshops and storytelling.

Product Strategy / Technology Hybrid

A product strategist with technology depth, who turns business intent into technically grounded direction and keeps feasibility honest.

  • Translate goals into well-formed requirements and user stories that engineers and AI coding tools can act on.
  • Build the technical fluency to discuss APIs, data, CI/CD and architecture trade-offs, and to plan scope, dependencies and capacity, including work done by AI agents.
  • Work with Engineering Residents to decide what to build, buy or skip, and to check what AI-assisted development produces.

A good fit if you are drawn to how things work under the hood, like structured problem solving, and want to speak credibly with engineers.

Not sure which one fits? That is normal. Tell us what you are drawn to in your application, and we will help you find your path during the program.

What you will do

You will contribute to a real product backlog, run light user research, and help make sure your team builds the right thing for the right users. Typical work includes:

  • Research and strategy. Combine market analysis, stakeholder interviews and AI-assisted synthesis to uncover product opportunities and test your hypotheses with real users.
  • Requirements and specs. Turn high-level goals and "fuzzy" concepts into precise requirements, user stories and context that both people and AI tools can build from.
  • Rapid prototyping. Use AI-assisted tools to turn ideas into prototypes or working demos, and put them in front of users early.
  • Agile delivery. Practice Agile principles with your team: backlog ownership, sprint rituals, and iterative, value-driven delivery.
  • Roadmapping and prioritization. Build outcome-focused roadmaps that balance vision, technical feasibility and constraints, and prioritize with evidence.
  • Verification and quality. Review AI-generated research, specs and code with a critical eye, and help define how the team will know the product works.
  • Storytelling and presentation. Turn complex data into clear narratives that win alignment, and present your team's progress and recommendations.
  • AI scouting. Explore where generative AI can speed up the team's workflow or unlock new value, and be honest about where it does not help.

description:
As the Software Engineering Resident, you are an AI-Native Engineer on Method's internal product team. The people who will use the product are your customers. You sit with them, understand the problem, and build the answer in front of them, working with AI agents that write much of the code while you own what ships.

You will work alongside the Product Management and Design Residents from the first conversation, not at the end of a hand-off. Together you shape the problem, write the specifications, and turn them into a working, shippable product.

This residency is practical. The tools will change between now and when you start, and again before you finish. The residency teaches what does not change: framing a problem, directing AI to solve it, knowing when the output is wrong, and being able to explain every line you ship.

Today, our internal product is built with React, TypeScript and REST APIs, using AI coding agents. Expect that to have moved on by the time you join.

The Engineering Resident role comprises three primary learning areas:

  • Build with agents: Break problems into specifications an AI agent can act on, direct the agent, and review, test and take ownership of what comes back.
  • Build in front of the customer: Prototype quickly with the people who have the problem, show working software early, and turn their reaction into the next iteration.
  • Keep the work trustworthy: Learn what may and may not be shared with which AI tool, keep a clear record of what the AI produced and who reviewed it, and never ship code you cannot explain.

Key Responsibilities (Learning & Contribution):

  • Discovery: Sit with the people who use the internal product, ask questions, and help define the problem before anyone writes code.
  • Rapid Prototyping: Use AI tools to put working prototypes in front of users in days, not weeks.
  • Specifications: Co-write user stories and acceptance criteria with the Product and Design Residents, written so that both a teammate and an AI agent can act on them.
  • Agent-Driven Development: Build features across the product (interface, APIs and data) by directing AI coding agents, and use those agents to find your way around the codebase quickly.
  • Judging AI Output: Review everything an agent produces. Test it, question it, and catch it when it is wrong.
  • Quality: Write and maintain automated tests, and use them as the check that agent-produced work does what the specification says.
  • Data & Privacy: Learn Method's rules on what data may go to which AI tool, and follow them without supervision by the end of the residency.
  • Provenance & Review: Keep a clear trail of what the AI produced, who reviewed it and what changed. Take part in code reviews with senior engineers (mentors), giving and receiving direct feedback.
  • Understanding What You Ship: Be able to explain how every part of your work functions. AI speeds up the building; it does not replace the understanding.
  • Cost Awareness: Notice what agent-driven work costs to run, and factor that into how you work.
  • Communication: Explain progress, trade-offs and technical constraints plainly to non-technical teammates and to the customer.
  • Sharing What You Learn: Bring what you discover about working with AI back to the wider Resident cohort.

Qualifications:

  • You have built something that works (coursework, a bootcamp project, a side project) and can talk through how you built it.
  • You have used AI tools (coding assistants, agents, chat models) to build software, and can describe a time the AI got it wrong and how you caught it.
  • Foundational understanding of core web technologies (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) and at least one modern front-end framework. React is preferred.
  • Familiarity with version control (Git) and GitHub or GitLab.
  • Comfortable working with people who are not engineers: asking questions, explaining what you have built, and hearing that it is not what they wanted.
  • Strong problem-solving skills and a proactive attitude toward debugging and fixing issues.
  • No professional experience required. We value curiosity, aptitude, and a passion for building things that work.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Currently pursuing or recently completed a degree in Computer Science or a related engineering field, or graduated from a technical bootcamp.

Marshall Wace's Asia Treasury team is looking for a technically minded undergraduate to spend 10 weeks mapping, documenting and improving the workflows that underpin Treasury operations in Hong Kong. You will sit at the intersection of Treasury, Operations, Execution and Technology -- learning how processes, systems and teams connect across the firm while producing practical outputs the team will use long after the internship ends.

  • Present findings to the team and deliver documentation suitable for onboarding and future process improvement

description:
Who we are

Neros is transforming a defense industry mired in costly, behemoth machinery—to circumvent a looming vulnerability gap, to give dismounted soldiers a fighting chance against tanks, and ultimately, to get as many humans off the battlefield as possible.

While consumer technology is evolving by bounds on the smaller-cheaper-better path, U.S. defense technology wallows in the large, centralized, and wildly expensive paradigm. Our air, land, and sea machinery budget is staggering; yet these large assets can still be vulnerable to very small weapons. When swarm technology comes into its own, the asymmetry will escalate. Nowhere is the pattern more glaring than in small unmanned aerial systems (sUAS)—drones. 

What you will be doing

As a Mechanical Engineering Intern at Neros, you'll join a fast-paced, multidisciplinary team designing best-in-class drones and the equipment that supports them. You'll work on one or more of our product lines, contributing to real mechanical design, testing, and manufacturing challenges that make an immediate impact. We're seeking driven engineering students who are ready to put their skills to work, grow new ones, and help advance Neros's mission of credible deterrence at scale.

Responsibilities

  • Design hardware to optimize for performance, manufacturability and cost
  • Gather requirements and translate these into defensible engineering architectures and decisions
  • Perform design trades by effectively leveraging 3D modeling software, FEA tools, prototyping, and engineering first principles
  • Create high quality engineering drawings
  • Root cause hardware failures and manufacturing issues
  • Work with the Manufacturing and Supply Chain teams on build instructions, production tooling/fixtures, and vendor selection
  • Plan and execute validation testing for your designs
You should have the following
  • Pursuing a BSE or MSE degree in Mechanical Engineering or related field
  • Prior experience in fast paced engineering/manufacturing environments, including internships, co-ops, and/or project teams
  • Strong engineering fundamentals and the ability to solve problems through first principles thinking
  • Experience with a CAD software such as Solidworks or NX
Nice to have
  • Experience piloting, working with, or designing UAVs (including as a hobby!)
  • Experience working in a high volume, cost sensitive industry like consumer electronics or automotive
  • Broad knowledge of manufacturing processes and their appropriate applications
  • Experience with packaging and integration of PCBAs, batteries, and RF components
  • Familiarity with electrical and electromechanical components like BLDC motors and optical sensors
  • Experience designing for harsh environments
  • Hands-on fabrication skills (general shop tools, manual machining, welding, CNC machining, etc.)

$55.00/hr USD

description:
Who we are

Neros is a defense technology company rebuilding America’s drone industrial base. We design and manufacture high-performance unmanned systems that are tested in combat, iterated at startup speed, and built at massive scale. Our team culture is fast, hands-on, and obsessed with closing the gap between design and deployment.

As drones transform the character of warfare, Neros is delivering the systems the West needs to compete on the modern battlefield and deter the adversaries of democracy. We’re hiring engineers, operators, and builders who want to move fast, take on extreme ownership, and get capability into the hands of warfighters in months, not years.

What you will be doing

As an Electrical Engineer Intern at Neros, you’ll work on hardware that flies. We build low-cost drones for the US military and our allies, and you’ll work on the same boards as the rest of the EE team, from schematic capture and part selection through bring-up, test, and root cause. You’ll also work directly with our AI-Native Electrical Engineer to automate how we design, check, and release boards. This role is for a recent grad or early-career engineer who wants real ownership and a lot of time in the lab.

Responsibilities

  • Assist senior engineers in the design of Printed Circuit Boards (PCBs), including schematic capture and component selection
  • Support the PCB layout process and participate in the bring-up and functional testing of new hardware
  • Build and test prototypes and breadboard circuits to validate design concepts
  • Perform hands-on lab work using standard equipment including but not limited to oscilloscopes, spectrum analyzers, power supplies, logic analyzers and network analyzers
  • Execute verification and validation (V&V) test plans, setting up tests and documenting results
  • Contribute to root cause analysis investigations under the guidance of senior team members
  • Utilize and develop skills in ECAD software (Altium) for schematic and layout tasks
  • Work with our AI-Native Electrical Engineer to build tools and agents that automate our design, review, and test workflows
You should have the following
  • Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering or a related field
  • Experience in a hardware or electrical engineering role (internship experience is a plus)
  • Proficiency with standard lab equipment (e.g., oscilloscopes, multimeters, power supplies)
  • Hands-on skills in soldering and wiring for prototypes and rework
  • Familiarity with at least one ECAD software package (e.g., Altium, Mentor, KiCad) is highly desirable
  • A strong desire to learn, a coachable attitude, and excellent problem-solving skills
Nice to have
  • Altium
  • Experience with embedded systems, particularly with STM microcontrollers or other ARM Cortex-M based platforms
  • Academic or project experience with RF concepts, including wireless protocols like LoRa
  • Familiarity with simulation software such as SPICE, or MATLAB
  • Experience writing scripts for test automation or data analysis in Python
  • Experience building tools with AI coding assistants (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor)
  • Knowledge of standard communication protocols like SPI, I2C, and UART
  • Exposure to circuits for handling analog video (NTSC/PAL) or digital video (MIPI, HDMI)
  • Basic C/C++ programming skills for firmware loading and board-level testing

$55.00/hr USD

description:

What you will be doing

As an Autonomy Software Engineering Intern at Neros, you will be a key hands-on member of our autonomy team, supporting the design, development, and testing of the software that flies our drones. Within our team we tackle a very diverse set of problems from perception, state estimation through guidance and navigation, simulation and the system that measures whether our algorithms work on the actual drone. This role is perfect for a current student or early-career engineer who is eager to learn and grow. By the end of the summer, you will have your own autonomy code running on a real drone, and you will get to watch it fly.

Responsibilities
  • Write autonomy software in C++ and Python that runs on the drone
  • Implement, test, and tune algorithms against recorded flight data and in closed loop simulation before they go on the real drone
  • Help build the tooling that lets us validate new functionality, like evaluation on recorded logs and in simulation

description:
Who we are

Neros is a defense technology company rebuilding America’s drone industrial base. We design and manufacture high-performance unmanned systems that are tested in combat, iterated at startup speed, and built at massive scale. Our team culture is fast, hands-on, and obsessed with closing the gap between design and deployment.

As drones transform the character of warfare, Neros is delivering the systems the West needs to compete on the modern battlefield and deter the adversaries of democracy. We’re hiring engineers, operators, and builders who want to move fast, take on extreme ownership, and get capability into the hands of warfighters in months, not years.

What you will be doing

Neros builds first-person-view drones for the modern battlefield. In just 2 years, Neros has built the highest rate drone production line in America, building over 1000 Archer UAVs per month.

Firmware is what makes those aircraft fly. Neros firmware engineers write the embedded software that runs on every processor in the system — the flight controller that keeps the aircraft stable, the radios that carry command and video, the ground station the operator holds, and the payloads the aircraft carries. Our systems are built on small, low-cost bare-metal microcontrollers and embedded Linux, and they are designed for high volume and low cost. Firmware is a key part of every Neros electrical system, so firmware engineers work very closely with electrical engineers.

As a firmware intern, you will own a real project on a real product — not a side task invented for an intern. You will write code that runs on hardware, debug problems that only appear on the bench, and see what you build fly. Neros firmware engineers own their work from start to finish, and interns are no exception: you'll help define what you're building, build it, test it, and hand it off working. Interns are placed on a team based on their strengths and what's in flight that term — flight controls, ground software, the embedded platform, or test and simulation.

Responsibilities
  • Write and debug embedded C/C++ on resource-constrained microcontrollers, or Python tooling that supports them
  • Bring up and test firmware on real hardware — flash it, instrument it, and find out why it doesn't work yet
  • Debug hardware-coupled problems using oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and serial traces — failures that don't reproduce in a debugger
  • Write unit and integration tests for the firmware you build
  • Work with embedded communication interfaces — UART, SPI, I2C, CAN, Ethernet
  • Use git and participate in code review: open pull requests, respond to feedback, and review others' work
  • Collaborate with electrical, mechanical, test, and manufacturing engineers to get your work integrated into a product
  • Document what you built so the next person can pick it up
You should have the following
  • Working toward a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field — or equivalent personal projects
  • Programming experience in C or C++, and familiarity with Python
  • Exposure to embedded systems — microcontrollers, development boards, or hardware projects — through coursework, personal projects, clubs, or prior internships
  • Hands-on instinct: you have built something physical that runs code, and you have debugged it when it didn't work
  • Comfortable with ambiguity — you can take a loosely defined problem and make progress without being told each step
  • Familiarity with git
Nice to have
  • Personal projects involving drones, RC aircraft, robotics, or embedded hardware — bonus if you can show us
  • Flight stack exposure — Betaflight, PX4, ArduPilot, or similar
  • Experience with an RTOS (FreeRTOS, Zephyr, or similar) or embedded Linux
  • Soldering and rework skills; comfort with a bench and test equipment
  • Test automation or CI experience — pytest, hardware-in-the-loop setups, or build pipelines
  • Controls or signal-processing coursework — PID, filtering, sensor fusion
  • Competition team experience (SAE, Formula SAE, RoboMaster, drone racing, CubeSat, rocketry)
  • Open-source contributions to embedded or drone projects
  • You fly — FPV, racing, or fixed-wing RC

US Salary Range

$55.00/hr USD

QuEra is seeking motivated interns to join our growing team focused on developing the calibration and performance characterization framework for QuEra’s neutral-atom quantum computers. As an intern, you will collaborate with physicists, software engineers, and hardware specialists to build and deploy automation tools that extract, analyze, and optimize key performance metrics from experimental data.

This internship offers a unique opportunity to gain hands-on experience at the interface of quantum hardware, data science, and software engineering, contributing to the development of scalable, reliable quantum computing platforms.

  • Verify physics models against hardware data to bridge the experiment/theory gap of machine characterization.
  • Contribute to tools for tracking and visualizing results.
  • Collaborate closely with physicists, engineers, and software developers to integrate your work into QuEra’s operational stack.
  • Participate in regular code reviews, documentation efforts, and team discussions around experimental strategy and system performance.

Qualifications

Required

  • Experience analyzing experimental or measurement data, including noise handling, curve fitting and model validation.
  • Familiarity of physics models of AOM systems, simulation of Hamiltonian time evolution, and error modeling of operations on the qubit subspace.

  • Enjoys hands-on experimentation, iteration, and uncovering structure in data.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.

Preferred

  • Familiarity with optimization or regression techniques (least-squares, nonlinear fits, Bayesian inference, etc.).
  • Exposure to laboratory instrumentation, data acquisition, or experimental control systems.

Education & Experience

  • Currently pursuing or recently completed a Master’s or Doctoral degree in Computer Science, Physics, Electrical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related quantitative field.

As an Apprentice Sheet Metal Worker, you'll develop the technical skills and craftsmanship needed to fabricate and install sheet metal components used in industrial environments. This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys working with their hands, solving practical problems, and seeing the results of their work.

You'll join a four-year, New York State-accredited apprenticeship program that combines paid, on-the-job training with classroom instruction, typically at Monroe Community College (MCC). Throughout the program, you'll learn from experienced professionals, receive performance evaluations every six months, and have opportunities for wage progression as you develop your skills. Successful completion of the program leads to a Journey Worker Certificate.

Through a combination of on-the-job training and classroom instruction, typically at Monroe Community College (MCC), you'll gain practical experience while working toward your Journey Worker Certificate. The program includes performance evaluations every six months, with wage increases following satisfactory reviews.

What You Get To Do

  • Learn sheet metal fabrication and installation techniques through hands-on training alongside experienced tradespeople.

  • Learn and apply welding and brazing techniques as part of your technical training.
  • Follow established construction site safety practices and develop safe work habits when using tools, machinery, and equipment.
  • Participate in classroom instruction and practical training to build the knowledge and skills required for New York State Journey Worker certification.
  • Build your technical capabilities and craftsmanship through ongoing feedback, hands-on experience, and performance evaluations throughout the apprenticeship.

What You Bring To The Team

  • High school diploma or equivalent, such as a GED or TASC.

  • A strong interest in learning the sheet metal trade and developing hands-on technical skills.
  • A dependable work ethic, willingness to learn, and commitment to producing quality work.
  • Ability to perform the physical requirements of the role, including climbing, working at heights, working in confined spaces, and lifting or moving heavy objects.
  • Ability to work in varying environmental conditions, including hot and cold temperatures and outdoor weather conditions.
  • Willingness to follow established safety procedures and learn safe construction and fabrication practices.
  • Reliable transportation to and from work and classroom instruction.
  • Flexibility to work overtime and travel occasionally as needed.
  • Ability to meet applicable pre-employment drug screening and background check requirements.

At Re:Build, our mission is to ensure the next generation of important products are made, at scale, in America. We are laying the foundation for a better future for our customers, employees, and communities by revitalizing America's manufacturing base and creating meaningful jobs across the country, including in historically deindustrialized regions. 

We operate an advanced, end-to-end manufacturing platform that partners with industrial companies and innovators to take products from first concept to full-scale production in critical verticals including aerospace and defense, electrification, medical, energy and environment, and robotics and automation.

At Re:Build Optimation, we specialize in delivering custom-engineered process equipment and automated systems to clients across the globe. Our multidisciplinary team of 70+ engineers, designers, and programmers, combined with 150,000 square feet of fabrication space and over 70 skilled tradespeople, allows us to provide full turnkey solutions—from initial concept through fabrication, installation, and commissioning.

At Re:Build Optimation, we believe in a collaborative approach, working closely with our clients to develop solutions that align with their unique operational goals. Our deep industry expertise and end-to-end capabilities make us the ideal partner for companies seeking cutting-edge automation, process control, and engineered systems.

What You’ll Learn

  • Project Overview: In memory-centric AI accelerators, many memory devices each process data in place and only exchange small partial results, which are then merged. As LLM attention evolves from grouped-query attention (GQA) to multi-head latent attention (MLA) and sparse top-k attention, the work done locally on each device shrinks while cross-device merge and reduction increasingly dominate decode latency. Using the team’s in-house performance model and simulator, you will explore the design space of merge/reduction architectures — where reduction happens, how devices are connected, and at what precision partial results are exchanged — and propose an architecture that performs well across modern attention workloads.
  • Skills You’ll Learn:
    • Architecture-level performance modeling and design-space exploration for distributed, memory-centric AI accelerators
    • How modern attention variants (GQA, MLA, sparse top-k attention) map onto distributed memory, and how they shift the balance between computation and communication
    • Hardware–software co-design of interconnect and reduction (collective) hardware for LLM inference

What You’ll Do

The AGI team at Samsung Semiconductor explores memory-centric system architectures for next-generation AI inference, where computation happens close to where data lives. We co-design hardware and software to make large-scale LLM inference faster and more efficient, and our work informs Samsung’s future memory and accelerator products. As an intern, you will own a research-driven architecture study end to end — from workload modeling to design-space exploration and an architecture proposal — working closely with architects and performance-modeling engineers, and you will present your findings to the broader organization at the end of the summer.

Chart Your Journey at Secretariat

From a collaborative culture to teammates who will always be by your side, find a career that will grow with you. Deliver your impact at Secretariat.

 

Secretariat is your source for independent expert advisory services.  Secretariat specialises in international arbitration, general commercial arbitration/litigation, forensic accounting, economic damages, construction, investigations and regulatory compliance and government contracting.  Secretariat’s experts maintain integrity, quality, and objectivity when solving complex disputes, delivering detailed analyses, and articulating meaningful results in a clear and concise manner.  

Secretariat’s team provides its clients and their legal teams with technical support to effectively navigate key aspects of the dispute resolution process. Our experts are adept at providing testimony and being cross-examined in arbitration hearings, mediations, and trials across the globe. Secretariat’s professionals have worked in industry and public accounting and bring a unique perspective to assist clients in growing their business and addressing complex issues.

Secretariat was recently ranked as one of the top 10 firms in Global Arbitration Review’s prestigious GAR 100 Expert Witness Firms’ Power Index, and over 90% of Secretariat’s testifying experts are recognized as leading experts in their field by the independent Who’s Who Legal. 

We are looking for an intern to join us our Brisbane office for a three-month period. Although our work and projects are varied, the type of tasks undertaken would likely involve assisting with the measurement and valuation of construction works, estimating the cost of making good defects, compiling and analysing data to support time-related and disruption claims, assisting with the response to analyses performed by other experts, and generally assisting legal teams in the preparation and presentation of their claim to national and international Tribunals and Courts.

Responsibilities:

  • Supporting our team who are primarily quantity surveyors acting as Quantum experts on construction disputes
  • Assisting in data research and analysis in drafting expert reports
  • Assisting in analysis or preparation of claims
  • Administrative duties to support the team

Requirements:

  • Currently in penultimate or final year of a Degree in Engineering, Construction or Quantity Surveying (and on track for at least a 2.1)
  • Strong skills using relevant software tools: MS Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Access).
  • Able to adapt to a dynamic consultancy environment.
  • Able to meet tight deadlines and work under pressure
  • Excellent communication and presentation skills
  • Any exposure to construction or engineering terms and concepts will be considered an advantage, but not required.

A rewarding career above all

There are a lot of fine consulting firms out there. But when everything is on the line, it takes a unique combination of skill and savvy to succeed under pressure.

Our culture and people are driven by passion, pride, and performance. Passion for the clients we serve, the work we deliver, and the communities we live in. Pride in our cohesive team recognized for excellence and trusted to perform in the most challenging situations. And our track record of outstanding performance across all of our disciplines speaks for itself.

Our people are motivated to be the best in everything they do – from our approach to making the complex simple to the way we mentor our up-and-coming talent to become trusted experts early in their careers.

Who We Are: 

Ai2’s Climate Modeling team (Ai2CM) has developed ACE, the world’s leading AI-based global atmosphere emulator for climate applications. ACE can be trained to replicate weather variability and climate change at 100 km horizontal resolution using historical observations or outputs from any physics-based climate model. It runs hundreds of times faster  on a single GPU than such a model running on a supercomputer. For climate-planning applications, we have implemented diffusion-based super-resolution for downscaling ACE simulations to kilometer-scale local detail. We also recently began a collaboration with Google Research to advance NeuralGCM, a hybrid AI-physics model, for climate projection applications.

At Ai2, you will be working with world-class AI researchers and software engineers. We perform team-based, ambitious research, with a mandate to strive for big breakthroughs, not just incremental progress, in an exciting and interactive workplace.

Interns will develop and apply novel AI methodologies for projects such as: (1) account for the effects of disparate radiative forcing agents including aerosols within ACE; (2) improve representation of land processes or the stratosphere in ACE; (3) improve the generalization capabilities of NeuralGCM’s column-wise learned physics.

You will work closely with a technical mentor on project design, coding and testing. Your technical mentor will discuss project details with you before your start date.

Over the course of your time at Ai2, you will build your resume and leave an impact on Ai2 and the world.  We have a beautiful office near a bike trail, the University of Washington and Lake Union; daily catered lunches; and great pay.  Summer is the perfect season to explore Seattle and our great outdoors.

About the Opportunity

Space is the newest contested domain, and True Anomaly is building the technology that keeps it secure. We design, build, and fly autonomous spacecraft and the software that gives operators real-time awareness of what's happening in orbit — work that sits at the intersection of national security, robotics, and space exploration.

Our Summer 2027 Internship Program puts you in the middle of that mission. This isn't a program of busywork or shadowing — interns are embedded on real teams and own real project work with real deadlines and real impact on programs that matter. You'll work alongside engineers, operators, and business leaders who are solving problems that don't have a textbook answer yet.

True Anomaly's 2027 Summer Intership Program will run from June 1st, 2027 - August 13th, 2027.

We're building internship opportunities across three tracks:

  • Engineering — hands-on work across disciplines like spacecraft systems, software, hardware, test, and mission operations.
  • Technical — cross-functional technical work supporting programs, data, and mission-critical operations.
  • Business — exposure to the business side of a fast-moving space company, including areas like program management, finance, people, communications, and strategy.

This is a general-interest posting to help us build our Summer 2027 candidate pipeline. As specific internship roles are finalized across teams and locations, we'll reach out to candidates in this pool whose interests and qualifications are the best fit.

What We're Looking For

  • Currently pursuing a degree (or equivalent hands-on experience) in a relevant field of study for your track of interest.
  • Genuine curiosity about the space and national security industry, and a drive to contribute to real project work, not just observe.
  • Able to work full-time (40 hours/week) for 10 consecutive weeks during the Summer 2027 program window.
  • Able to work in-person at one of our office locations: Denver, CO; Long Beach, CA; Colorado Springs, CO; or Washington, DC.
  • Able to independently arrange your own housing and transportation for the duration of the internship

Compensation

$30–$32/hour, depending on track, role, and experience. Eligible for relocation for the duration of the internship. 

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.

True Anomaly is committed to equal employment opportunity on any basis protected by applicable state and federal laws. If you have a disability or additional need that requires accommodation, please do not hesitate to let us know.

To protect candidates and our company from application fraud and impersonation, we use third-party tools to verify applicant identity and detect fraudulent applications. Learn more in our Privacy Notice.

About Wheely

Wheely is redefining premium transportation across major cities in Europe, the US, and the Middle East. We blend cutting-edge technology with the craft of five-star chauffeuring to deliver an experience trusted by more than 100,000 active riders and 1,200 corporate accounts.

We’re a profitable, fast-growing scale-up with $43M raised and over $100M in annual revenue. Having recently launched in New York City, we’re expanding rapidly across the US and EMEA. If you take pride in your craft and want to help shape the next chapter of our growth, we'd love to hear from you.

The Role

Wheely runs a high-frequency, luxury marketplace — precision isn't a goal here, it's the baseline. As an Operations Intern in Paris, you'll work inside the France Operations team across the full chauffeur lifecycle: acquisition, retention, and day-to-day chauffeur management. This is a flexible internship (3 to 6 months, depending on your need) available immediately or in the coming weeks (starting no later than early January 2027).

This isn't a coffee-and-slides internship. You'll carry real workstreams, with real stakes, from week one.

Why This Role

  • High-growth business. Wheely France is scaling fast and expanding into new markets.
  • Direct impact. Your analysis feeds decisions across acquisition, retention, and chauffeur quality — not a slide deck that sits in a folder.
  • Real exposure. You'll work directly with the Ops team and senior leadership on live problems, with room to bring your own ideas.

Responsibilities

  • Support chauffeur acquisition, retention, and day-to-day chauffeur management across the France Operations team.
  • Turn data into clear, actionable insights — root-causing issues, tracking initiatives, and flagging what's working and what isn't.
  • Prepare data pulls, dashboards, and analyses for the wider Ops and leadership team.
  • Act as a day-to-day Wheely representative to the chauffeur community.

Requirements

  • Currently enrolled in a top French grande école, école d'ingénieur, or university (final year or gap year/césure).
  • Comfortable with data and eager to build hands-on skills in SQL (no prior knowledge required, but is a plus).
  • A structured thinker who turns ambiguity into a plan, not a shrug.
  • Clear communicator, able to summarise a complex point simply.
  • Available for 3 to 6 months.
  • Fluent French and English.
  • Based in Paris, ability to work full-time in the office 5 days a week.

What we Offer

  • Office-based role in Paris (9th arrondissement)
  • Convention de stage obligatoire
  • Competitive salary of up to €1,800/month
  • Best-in-class equipment
  • Monthly credit towards Wheely journeys
  • Daily Lunch Allowance
  • Real ownership on live projects, working directly with the France leadership team

All of your personal information will be collected stored and processed in accordance with Wheely’s Candidate Privacy Notice

description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

AI TUTOR, MEDICINE - TEMPORARY

In this role, you will help enhance Grok by creating and annotating high-quality data across the field of medicine. You will draw on your clinical expertise to evaluate model outputs, identify errors in clinical reasoning, and capture how clinicians think, communicate with patients, and navigate complex medical decisions. Your work will help train Grok to distinguish unsafe or clinically flawed responses from guidance that is evidence-based, diagnostically precise, and consistent with the standard of care. This work spans text, voice, and video, including recording audio and participating in video sessions.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Use proprietary software to create, label, and annotate data on defined medical projects.
  • Produce high-quality data efficiently, with exceptional attention to accuracy.
  • Help design and launch new medical data tasks, working closely with colleagues and technical staff to bring cutting-edge initiatives to life.
  • Partner with engineers to improve the design of fast, efficient annotation tools.
  • Help put trustworthy medical information within reach of patients and users worldwide.
  • Improve patient outcomes by solving real healthcare problems that train Grok to meet clinical standards across decision-making, drug discovery, diagnostic imaging, and procedures.
  • Create and solve complex medical problems within your area of expertise, such as diagnostic reasoning, treatment planning, care coordination, or image interpretation, writing detailed reference answers and critically evaluating model responses.
  • Interpret, analyze, and carry out tasks based on evolving instructions.

POSITION DETAILS:

This is a temporary position with SpaceXSI, for the length of time as stated, and is subject to change with minimal notice as business needs dictate.

  • LENGTH OF POSITION: 6 months (extensions or conversion to a permanent role may be available based on business needs).
  • LOCATION: Remote (United States, United Kingdom, Canada, India, and Australia); for US-based candidates, please note that we are unable to hire in Wyoming and Illinois at this time.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • MD, DO, MBBS, MBChB, DNP, PharmD, PsyD, DDS, DMD, DPT, DPM, OTD, or DVM degree, or an international equivalent of one of those degrees; OR a master’s degree or Ph.D. in nursing, physician assistant studies, clinical psychology, counseling psychology, public health, epidemiology, biostatistics, pharmacology, or biomedical sciences.
  • 2+ years of employment experience in a clinical, research, or health-related role after the qualifying degree was conferred (completion of a residency or other postgraduate training is not required; residency, fellowship, and internship positions count toward the experience requirement).
  • English proficiency at CEFR C1 level or higher.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Skill at navigating medical literature, databases, and online resources.
  • Excellent communication, interpersonal, analytical, and organizational skills.
  • Sound independent judgment when information is limited, and the ability to explain your reasoning clearly to others.
  • A genuine passion for innovation and for using technology to improve patient care.
  • Multiple publications, or a first-author publication, in a reputable journal or outlet.
  • Prior data annotation or teaching experience (as a professor, teacher, or tutor).
  • Experience in technical writing, medical writing, journalism, or another professional writing setting.
  • Post-graduate clinical experience or equivalent real world experience.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • This role may be offered as a full-time or part-time position depending on role/business needs and candidate availability; full-time positions are preferred and require working standard business hours in your local time zone.
  • We are unable to provide visa sponsorship.
  • Must be willing to travel to a SpaceXSI site.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

You’ll lead an independent research project exploring approaches to sim-to-sim and sim-to-real transfer for sensor-based driving models. You’ll work with Toyota driving data, generative base models, and closed-loop simulation infrastructure, with the goal of producing work suitable for a conference or workshop submission. The Opportunity As a research intern on AD2, you will own a standalone research project in sim-to-sim and sim-to-real domain mapping, with the opportunity to: Drive your own research: Shape the approach, run experiments, and analyze results, with the independence to set your own direction. Publish your findings: The project is designed to produce results suitable for a conference or workshop publication. Shape a real autonomy model: The tools and insights you create will help the team post-train our autonomy model more effectively, with the potential to influence the autonomy stack eventually deployed in Toyota vehicles. Collaborate with experienced researchers: Work closely with a small team of industry-leading researchers with deep experience in robotics and autonomous driving. Work at scale: Use the same large-scale Toyota driving data, base models, and simulation infrastructure the team uses every day. The work will combine algorithm development with experiments in simulation and on real robots, emphasizing reliable adaptation with limited robot experience and human effort. The Research We are interested in how robots can improve through ongoing experience while preserving and building on what they have learned. Your project could explore one of the following directions: Continual learning: Preserve existing capabilities through successive adaptations and use prior experience to learn new behaviors more efficiently. Investigate how useful adaptations can be retained, combined, and reused, including settings where the original training data are unavailable. Efficient learning and adaptation: Enable robots to improve with limited experience by identifying where adaptation is needed and making effective use of prior knowledge, new interactions, and guidance. Personalization from human guidance: Use demonstrations, corrections, or preference feedback to change how a robot performs a task while maintaining task success. Investigate when guidance is sufficient and when further learning is needed. Possible approaches include reinforcement learning, imitation learning, agentic tool use, modular policies, and distillation, depending on the research question.

The Mission We are working to create general-purpose robots capable of accomplishing a wide variety of dexterous tasks. The intern who joins our team will be expected to create working code and/or hardware prototypes, interact frequently with team members, run experiments with both simulated and real (physical) robots, and participate in publishing the work to peer-reviewed venues. We’re looking for an intern who is comfortable working with both existing large static datasets as well as a growing and dynamic corpus of robot data.
